#814. Jeff Bezos Reveals Process of Casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond

After Robert Pattinson was announced as the next James Bond, Jeff Bezos reflected on the Amazon MGM casting coming on the heels of a tight race: “It was interesting.”

The choice of the next James Bond truly came down to the wire.

After Robert Pattinson was announced as the successor slipping into the role as the titular secret agent, Jeff Bezos reflected on the Amazon MGM casting process, noting the choice was made just days before the big reveal.

“We ran a really tight process and made the final decision on Friday [Nov. 13],” Bezos shared at the Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event, per Variety. “There was a big group initially, and we down selected to five finalists. We did real, old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists.”

Referring to the group of finalists—rumored to include Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, Jacob Elordi and Callum Turner—Bezos noted the process of elimination “was interesting,” adding that it involved “full costumes and real sets and other actors.”

“We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists,” the Amazon founder explained, “and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all the tests and reviewing all that.”

And though all five finalists were “amazing,” it was the Twilight star who truly had the team shaken.

“There was something special about Rob and his performance,” the 62-year-old said. “It was immediately undebated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director…we all gravitated toward Rob. Initially, we were slightly biased against him just because he’s already so famous, like maybe we should have somebody more unknown, but in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond.”

As for Pattinson himself, making the leap from spider monkey to special-ops enforcer is a move he deeply appreciates making.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson previous shared in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy [Pascal], David [Heyman], Tanya [Lapointe], and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

And no time is better than the present for a closer look at more roles that almost went to other actors...

Glen Powell as Tim Riggins on Friday Night Lights

The Top Gun: Maverick star tried out for multiple parts on Friday Night Lights, including the main role that Taylor Kitsch played.

The Star Trek actor lost out on the role, which ultimately went to Ben McKenzie, due to his bad acne.

"I had awful skin as a teenager," he said on Josh Horowitz's podcast Happy Sad Confused in May 2024, "and then I when I came after college, my skin started breaking out again."

"I was offered the role and it's probably my biggest regret, you know, on passing," the American Pie alum revealed in a 2021 SiriusXM interview. "I think I was in a phase of, at the time—it sounds so obnoxious to say right now—but at the time it was like, 'OK, do I want to do TV?' I don't know that I was quite ready to go that route."

Rob Lowe as Derek Shepherd on Grey's Anatomy

The Parks and Recreation alum revealed that he turned down the role of McDreamy in his 2014 memoir, and it came back up in an episode of Marc Maron's podcast.

"That's probably cost me $70 million," Lowe joked. "Eh, it's just money."

The actor added that he did watch the pilot when it came out and "when they started calling the handsome doctor 'McDreamy,' I was like, 'yeah, that's not for me.'"

The Sherlock star auditioned for the role of vampire Bill Compton back in the day. Stephen Moyer went on to land the part.

Before she was an Oscar winner, the Eyes of Tammy Faye actress read for the role of Sookie Stackhouse. The part eventually went to Anna Paquin.

The Hunger Games star read for the part of werepanther—and almost got the part—but her young age at the time played a factor in the part going to another actress. Lindsay Pulsipher landed the gig.

Tiffani Thiessen as Rachel Green on Friends

The Saved By the Bell veteran said she auditioned for the iconic role, but she was ultimately too young for the part.

Riverdale's Camila Mendes said the 13 Reasons Why star was one of the actresses who auditioned for the role of the iconic blonde. As she told Entertainment Weekly, "I remember we went out and we got falafel with a guy who was auditioning for Archie."

It's hard to imagine anyone else playing Capeside's resident NYC transplant, but as creator Kevin Williamson revealed to Entertainment Weekly, the role of almost went to the Grey's Anatomy star.

"She looked slightly older at that time. Even though she was younger, I just think she was more mature," Williamson recalled. "She gave a great audition, I remember we were all sort of like, ‘Wow, she's good.'"

However, the part ultimately went to Michelle Williams.

According to Williamson, the role of Dawson Leery's lovesick BFF was actually the Cruel Intention actress' to lost.

"I really loved Selma until, of course, I got the infamous videotape from the basement of the Holmes family in Toledo, Ohio," he said of Katie Holmes' last-minute auditon. "And when that video showed up, it changed my whole life."

The House star was so close to taking on the iconic role of Carrie Bradshaw that she even had a completed contract. In the end, however, she was just the back-up to the producers' first choice, Sarah Jessica Parker.

"I was either going to do it or not. It all depended on whether she said yes," Edelstein said. "My contract was complete. I was waiting."

Initially, The CW wanted the Full House alum as our favorite beautiful blonde Upper East Sider, but casting director David Rapaport only had eyes for Lively.

"I was terrified we wouldn't get her or they wouldn't like her," he told BuzzFeed, "because, honestly, the show lived and died on her and I had absolutely no other ideas."

The CW wanted Bruce Willis and Demi Moore's oldest daughter as the Gossip Girl lead, but casting director Rapaport knew she wasn't right for the role (and would eventually cast her on 90210).

"I love Rumer," he told BuzzFeed. "She's grown into quite an amazing actress and person, but that, to me, was based on protecting the investment of a television show where creatively, these lesser-known girls really captured the essence of the show and carried it for six years."

Alden Ehrenreich as Dan Humphrey on Gossip Girl

Rapaport told Entertainment Weekly that he "desperately" wanted the Star Wars: A Solo Story actor to be Lonely Boy, but producers thought he was too short to play Blake Lively's love interest.

Produces said nope to the Disney Channel alum because they felt she was "felt a little too young" next to Grant Gustin, who played the titular superhero, according to Rapaport.

The role ventually went to Candice Patton.

"We had seen Candice initially," he remembered, "but I think we were too early on in the process to cast her so we ended up testing Keke Palmer and this other girl."

Before the Battle of the Bastards, there was a battle between Rheon and Kit Harington for to actual role of Jon Snow.

"I auditioned for the pilot of Game of Thrones, and was down to the last two for Jon Snow," he told The Telegraph, saying that everything eventually worked out when he landed the role of season five villain Ramsay Snow.

"Ramsay is the complete polar opposite," he added. "In my mind, I secretly thought it was Ramsay."

After working with the Guardians of the Galaxy star on the final season of The O.C., Josh Schwartz revealed Pratt was his first choice for the role that eventually went to Zachary Levi.

"He was the first guy I wanted to play 'Chuck'. But as fate would have it, he was destined to guard the galaxy, not the Buy More," Schwartz revealed. "And might I add, couldn't happen to a nicer guy."

The Dawson's Creek veteran met with Orange Is the New Black creator Jenji Kohan early in the show's development, Kohan revealed. Holmes, who is an admitted fan of the series, had "other things to do," Kohan told E! News. "And also in the beginning no one knew what this was."

Yep, Robin Scherbatsky could have been Kate Austen, and two of our favorite shows were almost very different, according to Cobie Smulders.

Both she and Evangeline Lilly were "testing for Lost," Smulders revealed to E! News in 2014. "She owes a lot to me because I went in and I bombed the audition. And she was like, 'Thank you!'"

Everybody knows The Good Wife is Julianna Margulies' show, but that almost wasn't the case. The Emmy winner revealed the studio wanted Ashley Judd and Helen Hunt before she got the gig.

Katie Holmes as Buffy on Buffy the Vampire Slayer

Hard to imagine anyone else hunting down vampires in Sunnydale, but the Dawson's Creek actress almost had the title role in the WB series. Holmes turned it down to go to high school, and Sarah Michelle Gellar was cast.

Lorraine Bracco as Carmela Soprano on The Sopranos

Before taking her place in the chair as psychiatrist Jennifer Melfi, the Oscar nominee turned down playing mobster wife Carmela Soprano because she had portrayed a similar part in Goodfellas. The role eventually went to Edie Falco.

Taraji P. Henson as Olivia Pope on Scandal

Before she was breaking records on Fox's Empire, the Oscar nominee revealed she had auditioned to be Scandal's ultimate fixer, Olivia Pope. "When I went in to read for Shonda Rhimes, in my mind I was like, 'This is Kerry Washington. Why am I even in here?'" she said. "It was hers."

Gillian Anderson as Lady Cora on Downton Abbey

Can you imagine Agent Scully residing in Downton Abbey? It almost happened, but the X Files star turned down the role that eventually went to Elizabeth McGovern.

Ashlee Simpson as Elena on The Vampire Diaries

It's hard to imagine anyone else playing Elena Gilbert on the CW hit series, but the "Pieces of Me" singer was the network's first choice. It wasn't until the producers took a second look at Nina Dobrev's audition tape that they decided to go with the Bulgarian beauty.

Whitney Houston as Sondra on The Cosby Show

The legendary singer was offered the lead role in Bill Cosby-led series, but passed to pursue her music career. The oldest Huxtable daughter was ultimately portrayed by Sabrina Le Beauf.

Dana Delany as Carrie on Sex and the City

To Sex and the City fans, Sarah Jessica Parker is Carrie Bradshaw, but once upon a time, Delany was offered the role of the New York columnist. The Emmy-winner passed because she had already done multiple projects involving x-rated material (Nude Girls, Exit to Eden) and didn't want to be involved with a project that had "sex" in the title.

David Letterman's former late night show bandleader was offered the role by Jerry Seinfeld without an audition, but Shaffer never called him back. Jason Alexander was cast after submitting an audition tape featuring a Woody Allen impression.

AMC wanted the Boogie Nights actor, but Jon Hamm said during a podcast that Jane passed because he didn't want to be on a television show. Of course, Jane would go on to star in HBO's Hung.

#811. Fiona the Hippo Undergoing Medical Care After Eating Hat

Fiona the Hippo, the Cincinnati Zoo animal who went viral for her premature birth in 2017, is undergoing medical care after eating a knit hat that was thrown into her enclosure.

The Cincinnati Zoo confirmed that its famous semi-aquatic animal, who gained worldwide fame for her premature birth in 2017, is receiving medical treatment after eating a knit hat that was thrown into her habitat earlier this month.

“Her care team is cautiously optimistic that she will pass it and return to her usual self,” the zoo said in a statement Nov. 17, noting that Fiona is currently getting, “24-hour care and attention.”

After the zoo consulted with “veterinary and human specialists,” Fiona’s care team concluded that she is unable to undergo surgery to remove the hat. As a representative from the zoo acknowledged, “Our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she can pass it on her own.”

So far, Fiona is moving in the right direction. The hippo received a colonoscopy courtesy of The Columbus Zoo earlier this week as well as an ultrasound, which showed that her intestines are bunching, proving that she is working on passing something through.

In the meantime, Fiona is of course receiving all the love and support from her Cincinnati Zoo family, including “all of her favorite foods,” anti-nausea medicine as well as ensuring she stays hydrated.

“Fiona will remain off habitat until this is resolved,” the zoo added in a separate statement. “We will share updates as we have more information. Please help us keep our animals safe by securing your belongings and taking extra care near habitats.”

This isn’t the first time Fiona has fought an uphill health battle. The now-9-year-old hippo was born six weeks early back in 2017, weighing in at just 25 pounds, the lowest recorded birth weight for her species ever.

Ever since, Fiona has remained beloved in online circles, even participating in a virtual safari show as part of The Cincinnati Zoo’s programming during its shutdown for the COVID-19 pandemic.

As the hippo continues her latest health fight, the Ohio zoo expressed gratitude for all the love and support she’s received.

“As you can imagine, we are rooting for her,” the zoo added in a statement, “and hoping that she proves to be as strong and resilient as she was at the beginning of her life.”

For a look back at Fiona’s first moments in the world, keep reading…

The zoo's 17-year-old hippo named Bibi gave birth to little Fiona six weeks early on January 24, 2017. She weighed 25 lbs. less than the lowest recorded birth weight for her species, prompting critical care from vet staff.

Fiona's health made steady improvements in the weeks after her arrival, and by mid-March she had reached the 90 lb. mark, was eating hay and enjoying time in the pool!

Ever so curious about her surroundings, Fiona couldn't help but get an up-close look at herself on a computer screen.

By May, Fiona was well into the 200 lb. range and spending plenty of time lounging in her kiddie pool. What. A. Life.

Thanks to Fiona's tireless spirit and determination, she graduated to deeper-level pools after learning how to propel herself through the water.

It wasn't until early June that little Fiona began spending time with her mama. In the beginning, Bifi (as they were so lovingly dubbed) interacted during brief, supervised play dates but have since begun adjusting to life in the outdoor pool enclosure.

Fiona's dad Henry was reunited with his daughter one month later and from the looks of those hippo grins, their first time interacting went swell!

Fiona embraces all her curves and all her edges, and it's a much-needed reminder that we all should too.

It took much longer than anticipated, but Henry, Bibi and Fiona are finally cohabitating as a happy and healthy bloat. She can't get enough time exploring her dads' mouth, which is apparently normal behavior for a growing baby hippo!

Without a finalized schedule in place, Cincinnati Zoo visitors should cross their fingers in anticipation of seeing Fiona out and about. Here she is laying a wet one on her caregiver. Mwah!

This mother-daughter pair spends their afternoons splashing in the pool like any hippos should. And aren't those faces priceless?

#810. Wait, Feist’s ‘My Moon My Man’ Is Going Viral Again?

This week's Trending Up looks at another boost for the Canadian singer-songwriter's '00s favorite, as well as a couple rap songs taking off in recent weeks.

Welcome to Billboard Pro’s Trending Up newsletter, where we take a closer look at the songs, artists, curiosities and trends that have caught the music industry’s attention. Some have come out of nowhere, others have taken months to catch on, and all of them could become ubiquitous in the blink of a TikTok clip. This week: An ’00s Feist single goes doubly viral, a 2013 Gucci Mane song becomes a hit for the first time in 2026, and a rising British R&B artist scores a streaming breakthrough Related Noah Kahan Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nominations Snub: 'I Was In My Feelings for a Sec' 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Revs Its Engines & Leads 2026 Game Awards Nominations: Full List Cody Johnson on Why He's Skipping 2026 CMA Awards: 'Going 100 MPH All the Time Isn't Healthy' Explore Feist See latest videos, charts and news

To the ‘Moon’: Decades-Old Feist Indie Favorite Goes Viral for the Second Time in the Past Year

If you weren’t old enough to catch Feist‘s piano-pounding indie staple “My Moon, My Man” — or its block-rocking Boys Noize remix — back in 2007, chances are still pretty good you’ve been exposed to it by now. First, the song was used in a memorable opening montage sequence in the fourth episode of Canadian TV phenomenon Heated Rivalry‘s first season in late 2025, resulting in a huge streaming bump for the song that has mostly lasted through the 2026 calendar year. Now, it’s gone doubly viral, thanks to TikTok and FINNEAS.

The latter Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter covered the song for an Amazon Music original release back in September, in advance of Feist’s induction into the Canadian Hall of Fame. His version of the song has taken off as part of a couples TikTok trend with the “aaaaa”s from “my moon, my maaaaaaan” traveling from one slide in the post to the next. (Though according to reports, the trend is going just as viral for the people doing it wrong as those following the formula correctly.) It’s a complicated chain of events, as nearly every viral story is in 2026.

The result of it, however, is that Feist’s original “My Moon, My Man” — which never really stopped going viral from its Heated Rivalry bump nearly a year ago, still pulling in millions of streams a week — has now jumped up yet another level on streaming. For the seven-day period from Nov. 10-16, the song racked up over 4.3 million official on-demand U.S. streams, up 61% from the 2.7 million it notched the seven day period before that (Nov. 3-9), according to Luminate.

Meanwhile, the FINNEAS “Moon” remains an Amazon exclusive, so its streaming totals are more modest — but those have also seen a considerable uptick, notching 68,000 streams over that same Nov. 10-16 period, up 98% from the just-over-34,000 streams it collected the prior period. - ANDREW UNTERBERGER

From RAYE and kwn to Jordan Adetunji, Odeal and Sasha Keable, the UK R&B scene is one of the hottest enclaves in mainstream music — and Season 25 is making his case to be added to that list with his viral hit “Shotta’s.”

Season 25 debuted a snippet of the Tobiswag and Katzy-produced song in an Aug. 29 TikTok that has since garnered over 1.2 million views. Listeners immediately latched onto the song, citing elements such as its Partynextdoor-reminiscent production and lyrics that some described as “misogynistic.” “Look at how she treatin’, son, I know you’s a tender man/ When you call, she do not come, that is not your ho,” he sings at the top of the first verse. He officially dropped the song on Sept. 25, and it quickly became a favorite amongst TikTok influencers, fan cam creators and dancers. On Nov. 12, Billboard Hot 100-topping rapper Swae Lee brought Season 25 out for a surprise performance of “Shotta’s” at his London show.

According to Luminate, the song has explored by over 705% in streaming activity over the past five weeks. During the week leading up to his surprise appearance at Swae Lee’s show (Nov. 6-12), “Shotta’s” pulled in 1.83 million official on-demand U.S. streams, up 53% from the week prior (Oct. 20-Nov. 5), when it logged 1.19 million official streams. On TikTok, the official “Shotta’s” sound plays in over 3.4 million posts.

Last week (Nov. 12), Music Business Worldwide reported that Season 25 signed a deal with London-based indie label Isekai Records and New York-based broke Records off the success of “Shotta’s.” — KYLE DENIS

If you’re of a certain age, you’ll remember Gucci Mane and Lloyd’s “Fly S—t” collaboration from the ATL rapper’s 2013 Trap God 2 mixtape. 13 years later, TikTok has introduced the smooth hip-hop-meets-R&B joint to a new generation.

Most of the love is due to Lloy’d sultry hook, with that specific part of the song soundtracking a few disparate trends. Some users have used it for a dance challenge; members of the historically Black fraternity Kappa Alpha Psi have rallied around it to showcase their strolls (their Halloween posts were particularly popular), and others have hilariously pointed out that Lloyd’s voice sounds a bit like Steve from Family Guy. Searches for the song on TikTok were also driven by some users having difficultyfinding the song on Apple Music.

During the week of Oct. 23-29, the song pulled just 16,200 official U.S. streams. The following week (Oct. 30-Nov. 5), that figure leapt a whopping 1,296% to over 227,000 official streams. By Nov. 6-12, streams for “Fly S—t” jumped another 255% to over 806,00 official streams. That’s good enough for a two-week increase of 4,858%!

Trap God 2 tapped out at No. 20 on Top Rap Albums back in 2013, but maybe this “Fly S—t” resurgence could help it rewrite history. – KD

#809. Toney loses bid to avoid Euro 2028 court clash

Ivan Toney's trial will take place during the Euro 2028 tournament

A bid to move the date of England striker Ivan Toney's assault trial to avoid a clash with Euro 2028 has been refused.

The 30-year-old footballer, from Northampton, is accused of headbutting and punching Saber Da Silva during a confrontation at a nightclub in Wardour Street, central London, on 6 December.

Toney denied assault occasioning actual bodily harm at a court hearing last month and a date for a trial of up to four days was fixed for 12 June 2028, which is three days into the Uefa Euro 2028 tournament.

He represented England at this summer's World Cup and has made 10 international appearances. It is not yet known if he will be selected for Euro 2028, but the application was made in case.

At a hearing at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday, where Toney did not appear, his barrister Mozammel Hossain KC said: "It came to our attention thatâ¦ there may be potentially a football match called the European Championship in 2028 between 9 June and 9 July."

Hossain proposed a trial date in August that year, adding: "We ask you please that the matter be put back to then for a trial so that if the defendant is included in this football tournament he can play.

"My knowledge of football is very limited but I am told he was included in the last one in 2024 and the England squad for the World Cup."

Judge Tony Baumgartner called it a "speculative" application.

He refused the request, saying: "It does not seem to me to be in the interest of justice to disturb the date that was already fixed."

The judge said the application could be made again if Toney is selected for the England squad.

Toney missed out on the latest squad for the country's Nations League ties.

Toney started his football career with Northampton Town and played for teams including Wigan Athletic and Peterborough United before signing for Brentford in 2020.

He scored 72 goals during four years with the Bees before making a surprise switch in 2024 to Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli.

#808. England defender Carter joins Bay FC after Gotham exit

Jess Carter made 83 appearances across all competitions for Gotham FC

England defender Jess Carter has completed a move to Bay FC after leaving Gotham FC as a free agent.

The 29-year-old has signed a contract that will keep her with Bay FC - a club based in the San Francisco Bay Area - until 2028, with the option for an additional year.

Carter joined New York-side Gotham in July 2024 after a six-year spell with Chelsea that saw her win the Women's Super League on five occasions.

"Coming to Bay FC is a new challenge, and that's something I'm excited about," said Carter.

"I've been fortunate to be part of some successful teams, and I know how much work goes into winning. I'm looking forward to getting to know this group, earning the trust of my team-mates and doing my part to help us move forward."

Carter played in all 30 of Gotham's matches in 2026 as the club won the NWSL Shield - given to the league's regular-season champions.

She also helped Gotham win the NWSL Championship in 2025, when they defeated Washington Spirit in the final.

"Jess has been a big part of what we've accomplished as a club, and we're very thankful for the contributions she's made during her time here," said Yael Averbuch West, the president of football operations for Gotham.

Carter, who has 56 senior England caps, was part of the squad that won the 2022 European Championships, while she appeared in all six games as the Lionesses defended their title last summer.

"Jess has consistently demonstrated her quality in championship-winning environments at both club and international level," said Bay FC's chief football officer Paul Green, who worked with Carter at Chelsea.

"I've seen her development and the professionalism she brings every day. She will bring valuable experience to Bay FC, and we're delighted to welcome her to the club."

The 2027 NWSL regular season kicks off in February.

#807. Can global leaders put their money where their mouth is on climate?

World leaders warn that geopolitical divisions are distracting from the climate crisis as negotiations focus on clean energy and financing, while Iran calls for compensation for war-related environmental damage.

The slow international response to climate change has placed the world on a path to destruction, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told heads of state and government during opening statements at this year's COP31 climate conference.

"The ⁠brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us," he said, as world leaders gathered in the Turkish resort city of Antalya to set the tone for negotiations at the UN climate summit.

A UN reportlast month found ​the world will cross a temperature threshold countries agreed to pursue in order to prevent runaway global heating. At the same time, states like Germany are slipping down the rankings for climate action, according to the annual Climate Change Performance Index published Wednesday by New Climate Institute and Germanwatch.

Nonetheless, Guterres said the world has "the power to make sure the overshoot is a temporary breach."

Negotiators from close to 200 countries are meeting in Turkey at the end of a year characterized by extreme heat waves and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a flood, killing more than 1,400 people and leaving thousands more missing.

At this year's talks, national representatives are discussing climate solutions such as increasing the share of electricity in an effort to move away from fossil fuels.

On Thursday, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, one of the few heads of government from Europe's major economies attending the summit, said that the world's dependence on fossil fuels was at the heart of both the climate crisis and energy security challenges.

"The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security," he said, endorsing the conference's focus on electrification which he said would lower energy bills, create jobs and protect people from the volatility of fossil fuel markets.

Burnham promised a "new era of British leadership over the next decade," announcing the UK would put climate resilience high on the agenda during its G20 presidency next year.

The US, the world's largest historical emitter of damaging greenhouse gases, is not attending the summit — for the second year in a row after US President Donald Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement in 2025.

Other nations, including big polluters like Germany, France, Italy, Canada and Japan, also opted not to send their top leaders to the talks.

On Wednesday, Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who is hosting COP31 together with Australia, which is leading negotiations, called on developed nations to take greater responsibility on climate finance.

Financing disagreements center around who should pay for international climate action, whether funding should take the form of grants or loans and how to scale monetary support for developing nations. Many of these countries are among the most vulnerable to the climate crisis but have contributed very little to the emissions causing it.

Erdogan said while previous conferences had resulted in different ideas around financing, they have yet to be turned into action. "We set out to make this an implementation COP," he told leaders.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen addressed remarks that developed nations are not contributing enough to climate finance, saying that the transition away from fossil fuels is in "our common interest."

"Europe is the world's largest provider of climate finance. Last year alone, we contributed more than €32 billion [about $35.5 billion] to support developing countries," she said, adding that Europe will continue to support partners worldwide in tackling climate change.

A recent Carbon Brief analysis found that public funding pledged under the Paris Agreement to help developing countries tackle climate change fell by more than 70% in 2026.

Most multi-year pledges from donor countries expired in 2025. Since then, the US has stepped back from international climate efforts, while several European countries have cut their aid budgets, reported Carbon Brief.

Hilda Heine, president of the Marshall Islands in the Pacific, which face an existential threat from rising sea levels, said the response to overshoot "must be overwhelming" and quickly reversed otherwise "the world we know is over."

"Every fraction of a degree of warming brings more catastrophe," said Heine, adding that more warming makes it more difficult to adapt to living on a hotter planet, brings greater loss and damage from worsening weather extremes and greater financial need.

She called on leaders to triple climate finance by 2035 and make it easier for Small Island Developing States to access the money.

"We are told there is no money, but their spending on war grows; the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death. Replenish the climate funds," Heine said.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of a "solemn responsibility to this and to future generations ​to act," adding that this is the critical decade.

Australia, the world's third-largest fossil fuel exporter, has vowed to promote the views of the "Pacific family" — small Pacific nations in the region such as Tuvalu or Fiji, where pre-COP meetings were held in October.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Albanese said it was crucial that climate cooperation delivered practical results — "unlocking investment in clean energy technologies, accelerating electrification, speeding up action for our oceans, unlocking climate finance for those who need it ​most."

As reasons to speed up electrification von der Leyen pointed to wildfires in Europe and floods in Nepal, as well as droughts stretching from Central America to Sudan, and to the disruption to energy supplies linked to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

"The world is witnessing the cost of continuing with the status quo for our climate and our energy security," she said, adding that the European Union would double down on efforts to become climate neutral.

"Three-quarters ​of humanity live in countries that import fossil fuels, hostage to price shocks they did ​not create and cannot ‌control," UN Secretary-General Guterres said, adding that recent conflicts have made clear a shift to renewable energy would help improve energy security and the cost-of-living crisis.

Von der Leyen also expressed support for COP31's 35-by-35 electrification pledge. The pledge aims to increase electricity's share of final global energy use to 35% by 2035, with von der Leyen saying Europe would be the first "electro-powered" continent.

Heine of the Marshall Islands said electrification must must be strictly tied to renewable energy generation rather than fossil fuels, warning that continued oil, coal and gas extraction was a threat to her country's survival.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said his country wanted compensation for environmental damage caused by US and Israeli strikes, including oil leaks from attacks on tankers. The strikes began in February.

Iran, which is a major fossil fuel producer and has pushed back against strict language on phasing out oil and gas at previous COPs alongside other petrostates, has also struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

Pezeshkian linked the issue to climate finance and said his country expected "responsibility in times of war, to document and assess the environmental damages caused by military aggressions and to develop compensation mechanisms."

Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who hosted last year's COP in the Amazonian city of Belem, said the momentum for climate action had dropped off at the start of the year, partly due to the Iran war.

"We started talking more about weapons and tariffs than the survival ‌of future generations," he said.

He also warned that "climate agreements are the favorite targets of reactionary forces at COPs," and urged leaders to work together. Lula promised to protect the Amazon rainforest. "Brazil is back to defend the continuity of a healthy planet," he said.

This article was last updated on November 12 to reflect incoming statements from world leaders.

#806. El Coyote Earns Third Regional Mexican Airplay No. 1 With ‘Ranchero Enamorado’

It's the second chart-topper from the group's album Nacimos Pa' Ser Historia.

Sr. Charts & Data Analyst (Latin & Billboard Español)

El Coyote y Su Banda Tierra Santa earns its third No. 1 on Billboard’s Regional Mexican Airplay chart as “Ranchero Enamorado” jumps 2-1 on the list dated Nov. 21. The song is the second chart-topper from the group’s album Nacimos Pa’ Ser Historia, following “Te Dije” in July.

Released on Andaluz/FOMO/UMLE, “Ranchero Enamorado” climbs from No. 2 with 6.9 million audience impressions earned in the United States, up 6%, during the Nov. 6-12 tracking week, according to Luminate.

The song switches places with Los Ángeles Azules and Tini’s “Pa’ Él,” as the latter cedes the summit, dipping 1-2, after an 11% dip in audience impressions, down to 6.4 million.

El Coyote y Su Banda Tierra Santa’s ascent to No. 1 is the fifth time this year a group has taken the top spot from a collaborative track. Banda El Recodo de Cruz de Lizárraga’s “Sólo Tú” replaced La Arrolladora Banda El Limón and Juanes’ “Una Noche Contigo” at No. 1 on the Jan. 24-dated chart. Los Dos de Tamaulipas’ “El Chavalón” then took the crown from Xavi and Carín León’s “La Morrita” on the March 7 chart. Three weeks later, Calibre 50’s “Me Enamoré Solo” pushed “La Morrita” from the lead on the March 28-dated ranking. Meanwhile, Banda Los Recoditos followed on May 23, when “En Coma Inducido” took No. 1 from Banda Los Sebastianes de Saúl Plata and El Jerry Gerardo Coronel’s “Al Chile No Sé.”

Notably, before 2026, El Coyote y Su Banda Tierra last topped Regional Mexican Airplay in 2000, with “Te Soñé.”

“Ranchero Enamorado” also rises to a new No. 3 peak on the overall Latin Airplay chart, nearly matching its highest rank to date —among 22 entries— through the No. 2-peaking “Te Dije” last July.

Elsewhere, “Ranchero” gives the group its highest rank on the Hot Regional Mexican Songs list, where it rises 10-7.

#805. Why Christina Ricci Says Cher "Holds a Grudge" Against Her

Christina Ricci pulled back the curtain on her and Cher’s decades-long rift after they appeared in the 1990 film Mermaids together: “Unfortunately, she's still mad at me.”

If Christina Ricci could turn back time, she would patch up her relationship with Cher.

The Addams Family star revealed that while she and the Grammy winner—who starred in the film Mermaids together—once shared a close bond, their relationship is nonexistent today.

“Unfortunately, she's still mad at me,” Ricci told Andy Cohen on the Nov. 17 episode of Watch What Happens Live. “She holds a grudge.”

As for what turned their connection to stone?

“Well, when I was 19, I did some Rolling Stone thing, and they interviewed her,” Ricci explained. “Maybe it wasn't Rolling Stone. It might have been Première, but they interviewed her, and she said all these things that were not that amazing about me.”

In an effort to explain the quotes, the “If I Could Turn Back Time” singer attempted to reach out to Ricci.

“She left me a voicemail about how journalists are always trying to get the worst things, and blah blah blah,” Ricci continued. “And she was so sorry, and I was 19, and so I didn't return that message.”

And the Casper star believes their relationship is just as strained nearly 30 years later. As Ricci shared, “I've reached out to her since and gotten radio silence.”

E! News has reached out to a rep for Cher for comment but has not yet heard back.

Though the 46-year-old wishes she stood on firmer ground with the Burlesque star, she shared there’s no animosity on her end. In fact, she sees where the 80-year-old is coming from.

“I adore her. She's the best,” Ricci said. “And I absolutely can 100 percent imagine being Cher and being like, ‘Oh, my God, they misquoted me, and I'm going to call this young person and explain to her that they misquoted me.’ And then the gall of that young person to not return the call and be like, ‘Oh, my God, Cher, it's okay. I love you so much.’”

“Like, I would be so pissed,” she added. “I get it.”

That’s why her soft spot for Cher (real name Cheryl Sarkisian) persists.

“Love you, Cher,” she said. “I love you so much.”

Cher and Ricci played mother-daughter duo Rachel Flax and Kate Flax, respectively, in the 1990 coming-of-age film. And years later, the Penelope star shared how their familial bond wasn’t just for the camera.

“Cher took me under her wing, and she recognized that sometimes you could be on a set, and you don’t know exactly what is going on behind the scenes—power struggles, or different issues,” Ricci told Demi Lovato in the 2024 documentary Child Star. “And if you don’t know any better, and have no experience, you can think it was your fault. And she never wanted me to feel insecure."

But Cher and Ricci aren’t the only stars whose close relationship took a turn. Keep reading for more celebrity feuds…

The Sex and the City costars had dodged feud rumors for years, but they were reignited after Cattrall decided not to return for a third movie and made comments about her SLP that raised eyebrows.

"What was your reaction to Kim Cattrall telling Piers Morgan that you were never friends just colleagues?" Andy Cohen asked Parker on a September 2017 episode of Watch What Happens Live.

As she explained, "Just...heartbroken. I mean that whole week, you and I spoke about it because I was just...I don't know I found it really upsetting because that's, you know, that's not the way I recall our experience."

"So...it's sad but I'm kind of...I don't know, I always think that what ties us together is this singular experience is the thing," she continued. "It was a professional experience but it became personal because it was years and years of our lives. So I'm hoping that that sort of eclipses anything that's been recently spoken. That many years spent doing something so special that people had a connection with is such a privileged."

And though they didn't film scenes together, Cattrall did make a small appearance on And Just Like That.

During a 2022 TikTok challenge, JoJo Siwa described Candace Cameron Bure as the "rudest" celebrity, later explaining that she felt snubbed when Bure once refused to take a picture with her on a red carpet. Shortly after the dig, however, the Full House alum apologized: "I kind of broke your 11-year-old heart. I didn't take a picture with you. Ugh! I feel crummy, I feel—JoJo, I'm so sorry."

The two made amends. But months later, Cameron Bure was asked if she expects the Great American Family network, of which she serves as chief creative officer, to feature same-sex couples as leads in holiday movies. She said no, adding, "I think that Great American Family will keep traditional marriage at the core."

Siwa, who came out as a member of the LGBTQ+ community in 2021, wrote on Instagram that the actress' comment is "rude and hurtful to a whole community of people."

I love this girly life."

"I want people to know that Tan and I—we will be fine," he told Vanity Fair. "There was a situation, and that's between Tan and I, and it has nothing to do with the show. It was something personal that had been brewing—and nothing romantic, just to clarify that."

however, it seemed their hatchet was buried when Love replied, "Olivia - you're welcome. My favorite florist is in Notting Hill, London! Dm me for deets! I look forward to reading your note [winking face emoji]."

Since when has lip-syncing been live? Sorry about that, but I think everyone who lip-syncs in public on stage, when you pay like 75 quid to see them, should be shot."

#803. Israel row a 'defining moment for us' - Hallgrimsson

Heimir Hallgrimsson celebrates the victory over Kosovo with Harvey Vale

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson says the controversy surrounding the Nations League games against Israel has made "this group stronger".

The players took a vote on whether to play the two matches - in September and October - amid protests over the Israel-Gaza war, with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu making himself unavailable for selection.

The Republic of Ireland won the first match 3-0 in Hungary before a 1-1 draw in Serbia.

Hallgrimsson was speaking after his side defeated 10-man Kosovo 3-0 in Dublin on Tuesday night to finish runners-up to Austria in Group B3.

The second place means the Republic of Ireland will be in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw next month and also ensures they have a promotion/relegation play-off in March against a League A team as they try to move up to the top tier for the first time.

"It tested everyone - physically, mentally and no I've learned a lot doubt and the players have learned a lot and grown," said Hallgrimsson.

"I am pretty sure in one year, two years when this team becomes successful we will look back and say that was the defining moment for us.

"I am pretty sure we will look back in hindsight and say this was a huge moment for us.

"Us as leaders sometimes artificially create us against the world to get the group to stick together and I have said we have got that environment for free for two or three weeks and we survived it and it made this team and this group stronger."

Republic of Ireland seal second with win over 10-man Kosovo

Talisman Parrott caps dream year with two more goals

Republic of Ireland denied by Israel in draw

Troy Parrott scored two penalties and Jack Moylan also netted against a Kosovo team hit by the dismissal of Kreshnik Hajrizi after 26 minutes.

It brought to an end a campaign which saw the Republic of Ireland win two matches, with two drawn and two lost.

"We know we will never be perfect and we are trying to find a way to win with what we have," Hallgrimsson added.

"I think we are getting better and better on that. Like I said in the first meeting when I was here and was introduced, I said I want to build a team that is difficult to play against and I feel like we are getting closer and closer to that.

"We are now consistent in our selection of players. We've more or less found our squad, our group and with doing that on a consistent basis, playing the same players together, playing the same system, the connections between players are starting to emerge."

The promotion/relegation play-off draw take place on Friday with the Republic set to go up against one of Croatia, Serbia, Denmark or Wales.

"Everybody, and especially us, like to play the top teams. For one, to compare yourself with the best teams, that's one thing," he said.

"Second, those teams will expose your weaknesses and that helps you in your growth to play these teams and they will expose your weaknesses so we can continue our growth. We're already looking forward to March.

"[There are] exciting teams in the pot. Whoever we draw, it's going to be two tough games and it's good for this team at this time to play these matches instead of friendlies, for example.

"So we're really excited for March and looking forward to meeting the players again."

#802. Jennifer Lopez Addresses "Disappointing" Divorce From Ben Affleck

Nearly two years after Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck finalized their divorce, the "Let's Get Loud" singer looked back at the aftermath of their "disappointing" breakup.

Jennifer Lopez knows that sometimes, love does cost a thing.

Nearly two years after the "On The Floor" singer and Ben Affleck finalized their divorce, she reflected on the weight of their breakup—and whether she's ready to dance again with someone new.

"I'm done with that part of my life," Lopez said on the Nov. 17 episode of Benny Blanco and Lil Dicky's Friends Keep Secrets podcast. "It was such a hard, disappointing last situation on every level. On every level, it was so disappointing. I don't ever want to delve into that."

Though she is focusing on living life single, that doesn't mean she'll never be ready for another great love story, especially after taking a deeper look at her split from the Oscar winner.

"I'm OK with myself," she explained. "I was a serial monogamist, one after the other, trying to find the thing, hoping that this was it."

Now, the 57-year-old—mom to 18-year-old twins Max and Emme with ex-husband Marc Anthony—is getting loud with advice for others navigating divorce.

"Always operate in a way that you'll feel proud of when you look back," she shared. Looking back at her experiences, she added, "Even as painful as some of them were so bad—life-shifting pain and hurt—I can look back and be like, 'I loved completely. I acted in a way that I was proud of as a human. I didn't treat anybody in any way that I would be ashamed of.'"

"I did the best that I could in the moment with what I knew," she continued. "That's my advice for anything because when you go through hard things like that, it's easy to be like, 'F--k this.' You're in so much pain you want to hurt somebody else, or somebody has hurt you so much, but you can't. I've always held myself to that kind of standard."

Since then, Lopez—who filed for divorce from Affleck in August 2024, exactly two years after they got married—has continued to carry what she learned from their breakup and its aftermath.

"Be the best person that you can be right now, every single time, especially when it's hard," she emphasized. "When you say you're strong, I think that's part of it. I can look at these things and be like, 'It's OK. These are experiences in my journey.'"

"I don't know why it was my journey sometimes," she admitted. "Then I realized, no, I'm here to learn something. I finally got to a place where I feel like I've learned it, but it took the f--king house to fall down on top of me to do that."

Looking ahead, the "Let's Get Loud" singer—who was first engaged to Affleck in 2002 before splitting two years later—will be dancing for her papi when the time is right.

"I'm different," she said. "Because it changed me. Because I allowed it to change me. Because I wanted to learn the thing. I was like, 'It's done. I'm not doing this anymore. What are you going to do different?'"

"You can intellectually be a smart person and know things," she explained. "But the knowing is not the thing. It's changing the behavior and the patterns. That's the thing. And that is a conscious action that you have to do. You have to change."

#801. The Mavericks Band Members ‘Saddened’ by Name Rights Lawsuit From Raul Malo’s Widow

Paul Deakin, Jerry Dale McFadden and Eddie Perez say Betty Malo has been paid handsomely for their current tour.

The remaining members of Americana band The Mavericks have responded to a lawsuit brought by the widow of their late frontman Raul Malo.

Drummer Paul Deakin, keyboardist Jerry Dale McFadden and guitarist Eddie Perez wrote in a social media statement on Wednesday (Nov. 18), “We were saddened to learn that Betty Malo filed a lawsuit against us.” Betty sued the trio last week, alleging they should be prohibited from performing as The Mavericks following her husband’s 2025 death from cancer.

The crux of Betty’s lawsuit is a clause in the Mavericks’ operating agreement stating that the band could only use that name so long as Raul was involved. She says the surviving members are now violating this by touring with guest singers as “The Mavericks & Friends.”

Attorneys for Deakin, McFadden and Perez claim they amended The Mavericks’ operating agreement before their current “The Music Lives On” tour to remove such restrictive language. And in Wednesday’s statement, the musicians say Betty is actually being paid handsomely for these shows.

“To clear up any speculation on this topic, we have honored the financial agreement reached with the Malo estate before the tour began, and to date, Betty has received more compensation from the tour than any individual partner in The Mavericks,” wrote the band members on social media. “We’ll continue to honor this agreement, just as our ‘Music Lives On’ Tour has honored the music and legacy of our brother Raul at every turn.”

Betty’s lawyers did not immediately return a request for comment on the band’s statement Wednesday.

Legal disputes over band name rights are not uncommon in the music industry. In the past, such melees have broken out between the members of Stone Temple Pilots, Journey, Jefferson Starship and The Beach Boys. As Billboard previously reported, the question of who truly constitutes the band can be a thorny one, especially when groups change lineups over the years or operate under a web of contracts and LLCs.

As one expert put it to Billboard, “There can be a real disparity between the legal answer, about who owns the trademark, and the emotional answer as to what the name of the band means to the members and to the public.”

#800. Ward close to new Republic of Ireland deal as World Cup chance beckons

Carla Ward was appointed Republic of Ireland manager in January 2025

Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward says she is close to agreeing a contract extension, as she named her squad for their 2027 Women's World Cup play-off final with Poland.

The former Aston Villa manager replaced Eileen Gleeson at the helm in January 2025 and has led the side to promotion to League A in the Nations League and their highest ever position in the Uefa rankings.

The Republic of Ireland have lost just one of their past six games and now face Poland in a play-off for a spot at the World Cup in Brazil next summer.

Ward's side travel to Gdansk for the first leg on 1 December before the reverse fixture four days later at Dublin's Aviva Stadium.

The 42-year-old's current deal expires at the end of the 2027 World Cup qualification cycle.

Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said earlier this month that there were "live conversations" around Ward's contract.

"I want to get one thing straight - last time I said I wanted to focus on the next four games," said Ward.

"What I mean by that is, I want the focus to be on the players and certainly not myself.

"But what I can say to everybody is, I think you all know that I love being here. I want to be here. I have absolutely no intention of going anywhere.

"Thankfully, the FAI feel the same. So yes, just to echo David's words, we're close. And look, we're happy. I'm happy. So, yeah, I'm sure you'll have me for a little bit longer."

Ward in talks over Republic of Ireland contract extension

Two down, two to go - Irish target back-to-back World Cups

Republic of Ireland to 'lock in' for World Cup dream

Saoirse Noonan returns to the Republic of Ireland squad for the Poland games after sitting out the play-off semi-final victory over Kazakhstan because of an ankle injury.

The Watford forward comes in for Jess Ziu, who has a shin injury, in the only change to the squad.

Ward said that "now is not the time for trying new things" with the squad, which includes Crystal Palace midfielder Shanade Hopcroft after her first call-up for the Kazakhstan games.

Republic of Ireland secured 3-1 and 1-0 victories over the Poles when the sides met in World Cup qualifiers in April.

Poland edged out Belgium on penalties in their semi-final and Barcelona striker Ewa Pajor poses a dangerous attacking threat.

"They're a top side, they're a really good side," added Ward.

"They've proven that. They've got arguably one of the best forwards in the world and I think that their performance against Belgium was superb, home and away. I think they were excellent.

"They created a lot. We're under no illusions that this is going to be easy because we've won two games of football against them.

"I think both sides will tweak a few things naturally because we'll both want to try and win the game. But I go back to if we focus on us, what we're good at, if we execute our game plan and everything we want to do, then I think that we can win the game."

#799. Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17

At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

If you watch the Bundesliga, then you'll know Wael Mohya is a fast-footed, quick-thinking footballer. But not even the 17-year-old (Mohya turns 18 on December 31) Borussia Mönchengladbach youngster would have expected to be called up to the Germany squad so soon.

"Of course, I was absolutely thrilled. It means a great, great deal to me. I think everyone dreams of being selected for the national team at some point," Mohya said.

"And the fact that it's come to this now is, of course, just awesome and makes me very proud."

Mohya was at the gym when the call came in. He then shared the good news with his parents over dinner. "They started crying," the teenager said in a video posted on Gladbach's social media channels.

The youngster, who was born in a small town east of Düsseldorf, smiles and laughs a lot in interviews. He is always friendly, and in a good mood. On the field, too, he exudes the lightheartedness and carefree spirit of a 17-year-old.

As a technically skilled and creative player, Mohya often seeks out one-on-one situations and puts his opponents under pressure with quick dribbles. In nine Bundesliga appearances this season, Mohya has scored twice and delivered one assist.

"He's so cool and just plays really well. It's fun to watch him," Borussia coach Alexander Blessin said recently.

"Wael brings a lot to the team with his laid-back attitude on the field. He's not afraid to take risks, no matter how much pressure there is," added Gladbach's sporting director Rouven Schröder at a talk show on Sport1.

Borussia Mönchengladbach has been Mohya's sporting home since he was seven years old. Last season, previous head coach Eugen Polanski promoted him to the first team, and in December 2025, Mohya made his Bundesliga debut. Against Wolfsburg, aged 16 years and 347 days old, he became the youngest Bundesliga player in the club's history.

Mohya also recently completed a voluntary social year at an elementary school in Mönchengladbach. This is a program in Germany for young people who volunteer in the social sector — at hospitals, schools, or nursing homes, for example — for about six to 18 months. They gain work experience, help others, and earn a little money.

At the school's open all-day care program, Mohya helped serve meals, assisted children with their homework, and played with them. That's also where his nickname comes from. Because a girl hadn't understood his first name correctly or couldn't pronounce it, she called him "Waffel." Now, that name has stuck.

Even before being called up to the Germany team, clubs in the Bundesliga and across Europe's top leagues had taken notice of Mohya and were trying to sign him. His contract with Borussia Mönchengladbach runs through 2028.

With Gladbach currently in a relegation battle, his future appears likely to be elsewhere. If the club wants to generate transfer revenue from its biggest talent, next summer would likely be the opportunity to sell him — unless he extends his contract with Borussia.

The 17-year-old's career is managed by his parents. Whichever club can convince them that their son is in good hands and help him reach his full potential likely has the best chance of securing Mohya's signing.

Mohya himself says he doesn't even know how much he's currently earning at Gladbach.

"My parents take care of all that," he told Bild recently. "I get a monthly allowance, which is more than enough for me."

Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp recently revealed how much he had enjoyed his conversations with the youngster.

"The conversations I had with him were great," Klopp said with a laugh. "I wasn't that confident at 17, but then again, I wasn't that good either."

Since Mohya's parents are from Morocco, their son also holds Moroccan citizenship. As a result, he could have played for Morocco, but he has now decided against it. In fact, the Moroccan football association had been actively courting Mohya as early as last year and had already reached out to him in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup.

Now, like Frankfurt's Younes Ebnoutalib, Mohya will continue to play in the German jersey, unlike Schalke's Soufiane El-Faouzi, who chose Morocco, or Bayer Leverkusen's Ibrahim Maza, who likely would have been selected by Klopp as well if he hadn't already opted for Algeria.

For Mohya, who played for Germany's youth teams from the U16s through to the U21s, the door to Morocco remains open, even if he does play for Germany. According to FIFA regulations, players under the age of 21 can change national teams before their fourth international match (whether a competitive or friendly match), provided that none of those matches take place during a World Cup or a continental tournament such as the European Championship, Copa America, or Africa Cup of Nations.

If Mohya plays in the upcoming UEFA Nations League games in Serbia or against the Netherlands, another record is on the horizon. Although there were two even younger players who made their debuts in the Germany jersey — Willy Baumgärtner in 1908 (at 17 years and 104 days) and Marius Hiller in 1910 (at 17 years and 241 days) — the era in which they debuted is hardly comparable. And so, while Wael Mohya would rank third overall on the list, he would become the youngest Germany player in the modern era. The youngest to date was Hamburg legend Uwe Seeler in 1954, aged 17 years and 345 days.

#798. From kit boy to manager at 28 - Dumbarton appoint Fellowes

Martin Fellowes has become the youngest manager in SPFL history, taking on the Dumbarton head coach job at the age of 28.

Leaving his position as assistant manager and head of football operations at Scottish League 2 leaders Stranraer, Fellowes inherits a team six places further down the ladder.

With experience on the Scotland Under-19s coaching team, Fellowes spent almost 10 years with East Kilbride, rising from teenage kit boy to a two-month spell as interim manager in 2023, winning the Lowland League Cup.

With a day job in office furniture sales, he holds a Uefa A licence.

"You have to earn people's respect as a person," Fellowes told BBC Scotland.

"When you are a young guy and you're leading a football club, I don't think you can come in and change everything and lead with an iron fist.

"You have to get people's respect on and off the pitch. I know there will be plenty of criticism and there will be plenty of people sitting here today doubting that I'm capable of doing this job at 28.

"But now really the work for me has started on, by the end of the process, having gained those people onside to say, 'he was more than capable of doing this job and we're delighted to have him here'.

"I can only do that through winning games of football."

Martin Fellowes (right) as a 17-year-old kit man at East Kilbride

Jim Duffy was 29 when he began his long managerial career at Falkirk and Rhys McCabe was player/manager at Airdrieonians at the same age.

Ian Cathro, now leading French club Saint-Etienne, took charge of Hearts when he was just 30.

Fellowes replaces Frank McKeown, who resigned last month, while director of football Danny Lennon had been standing in on an interim basis.

The Sons are two points off the promotion places and visit Spartans on Saturday.

"We're not going to reinvent the wheel," Fellowes added.

"We're not going to do anything that anybody else hasn't been doing.

"But if we can add the 5% to every different department and win games of football, I think over time people will understand that sometimes the age isn't a barrier but it can actually be an advantage."

#797. Isaiah Washington Debuts New Romance One Year After Wife’s Death

Grey’s Anatomy alum Isaiah Washington revealed he’s in a new relationship with content creator Kei Bennett one year after his wife Jenisa Garland’s death: “She is all mine now and I am all hers."

It’s a beautiful day for Isaiah Washington’s personal life.

More than a year after the Grey’s Anatomy alum shared wife Jenisa Garland had died suddenly in June 2025, he detailed his next chapter with content creator Kei Bennett.

“I have known many incredible women in my life,” Washington wrote on Instagram Nov. 17 alongside a photo of the new lady in his life, “but not a single one of them can hold a candle to the deep Southern charm of @keibenet.”

“I am not only thrilled to have gotten to know her in the last 9 months talking to her for hours every single day,” he wrote, “I am absolutely baffled how any man in her past could have harmed her, belittled her, disrespected her, or even betrayed her in the most deplorable ways.”

As for how she’s pulled at his heart strings?

“She has an incredible mind, heart, and spirit and I have grown to respect her intelligence, green thumb, hair stylist talent, entrepreneurship, holistic approach, and her black business owner's business acumen immensely,” he explained. “Yes, she has earned her place at my creative table and I love her dearly.”

And while Bennett may have kissed her fair share of frogs in the past, he feels they were all leading to her prince.

“I am so glad that all of the men who treated her like she was less than a Queen, all left her heartbroken, but not broken,” he wrote. “Don’t worry I will take it from here and I will never let her down as a friend and partner in love and creativity.”

“There has been no other woman who has made me laugh and has encouraged me as she has,” he added. “Yeah, I don't play about Kei Bennett, and just know that she doesn't play about me. Yeah…she is all mine now and I am all hers. Deal with it.”

And it’s clear Bennett is just as smitten, commenting under the post, “I love you to pieces. Thank you for this. My protector, my best friends, my love, Mousie’s poppop…you exceed every goal you set and have the most pure heart I’ve ever seen.”

The couple’s hard launch comes after Washington’s wife of 29 years died following a weeklong health battle in June 2025. Just last month, he shared deeper insight into the tragedy.

"It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family," Washington—dad to kids Isaiah, Tyme and Iman with Garland—captioned his Oct. 3 Instagram post. "She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered."

And while her death came as a shock to their family, Washington shared how grateful he was to have his three kids by his side during the devastating chapter. As he put it, "She has been gone 16 months now, but she left 3 incredibly amazing children behind to continue her legacy."

For a closer look into the love lives of more Grey’s Anatomy stars, keep reading…

After being introduced in 1995, Isaiah Washington knew pretty quickly that he wanted to scrub in with Jenisa Garland, the two tying the knot one year later.

"For me, being married and having children did change a lot of my trajectory," the actor, who starred as renowned cardiothoracic surgeon Preston Burke for three seasons of Grey's Anatomy, told Fox News Digital in 2022. Sadly, their 29-year marriage came to an untimely end when Garland—who shared kids Isaiah, Tyme and Iman with Washington—passed away in 2025.

"It came as a huge shock to me and our entire family," Washington wrote in an October 2026 Instagram post. "She succumbed to a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered."

But more than a year after the tragedy, Washington found love again with content creator Kei Bennett.

“She has an incredible mind, heart, and spirit and I have grown to respect her intelligence, green thumb, hair stylist talent, entrepreneurship, holistic approach, and her black business owner's business acumen immensely,” he explained in a November 2026 social media post. “Yes, she has earned her place at my creative table and I love her dearly.”

Looks like it was record producer Chris Ivery who asked series lead Ellen Pompeo to pick me, choose me, love me after they crossed paths at a Los Angeles grocery store in 2003.

"I was with my mutual friend," the actress—who's starred as Meredith Grey since the series' 2005 premiere—detailed during a 2022 appearance on The Drew Barrymore Show.

So, after sharing a quick hello with her fellow Boston-area native, "He called me a bunch of times, and I wouldn't call him back. And then he said, 'You're rude. You won't call me back,' and I said, 'Well, because I'm not trying to go on a date with you.' And he said, 'Who's trying to go on a date with you? I don't even know you.'"

Basically, she continued, "We had a fight first. That's kind of always the way to my heart, is like, piss me off and I'm all yours."

Married four years later, the pair welcomed daughter Stella in 2009, her little sister Sienna in 2014 and son Christopher in 2016.

"We're sort of two kids who made it out and then landed in Hollywood and jumped on this ride," Pompeo said of their journey during a 2025 appearance on Alex Cooper's Call Her Daddy podcast. James Pickens Jr.'s starting line with wife Gina Taylor-Pickens dates back to the 1980s when the then-struggling actors met through the New York City theater scene. "I thought she was cute," the future chief medical officer Richard Webber explained to TV Fanatic, "and she gave me her number."

A stroll through Central Park proved to be the first steps of their forever. "We have a mantra that we've lived by for 35 years," the dad to Carl and Gavyn explained of the Deliver Us from Eva actress on a 2019 episode of Live with Kelly and Ryan. The romance between E.R. Fightmaster's neuroscientist Kai Bartley and Caterina Scorsone's neurosurgeon Amelia Shepherd may have been cut short during season 19, but as a wise woman once said, "If you aren’t willing to keep looking for light in the darkest of places without stopping, even when it seems impossible, you will never succeed."

#795. Joe Jonas Reveals Cheeky Gift He Recently Gave Ex Demi Lovato

Joe Jonas recently revealed that he gave Demi Lovato, whom he dated briefly in 2010, a cheeky birthday gift that nodded toward one of her most viral interview moments.

Joe Jonas’ favorite meme? He would have to say mug.

More than 10 years after Demi Lovato went viral for revealing mugs were her “favorite dish” during an interview with NRJ Berlin, her Camp Rock costar—whom she dated briefly in 2010—revealed it’s still his favorite pop culture moment.

“It’s amazing,” Joe told his brothers Kevin Jonas and Nick Jonas during the Nov. 17 episode of their Hey Jonas! podcast. “I bought her a mug as a gift for coming as our special guest recently or her birthday. I think I sent her a mug for her birthday. I can’t remember.”

Meanwhile, Kevin and Joe agreed it was a great clip.  As Kevin emphasized, “She wasn’t incorrect.”

For Demi’s part, she recently revealed that she intentionally had misinterpreted the question—the interviewer was referring to food rather than cookware—but she opted to answer it in her own way.

“I had been asked so many questions that day,” Demi reflected during an appearance on Keke Palmer’s Baby, It’s Keke Palmer podcast in March. “I was doing, like, a press tour and you get bored doing press tours.”

And so, the Disney Channel alum joked she thought at the time, “‘I’m gonna start f--king with the interviewers.’”

“I just ran with it,” Demi joked, emphasizing that only part of the interview went viral. “In the long, extended video, you see me look at my tour manager and like smirk. Like, ‘did you catch that one?’ And then that went viral and everyone thought I was serious.”

But there’s nothing wrong with being confident in answering the question this way, especially given Demi made a worthy case for mugs.

“I like mugs because they’re very comfortable in your hand,” she said in the now-viral clip. “And they hold hot things that you don’t have to touch. So, you know, coffee or hot tea.”

As for Joe running so far with the joke that he sent his ex a mug as a present? While Demi previously joked she was “mad” at Joe following their breakup, there’s no longer any mean mugging between them.

“It’s been such a wonderful relationship through so many years,” Joe told USA Today earlier this year after he and Demi each made appearances at each other’s respective concerts. “I feel so grateful that Demi and I can go perform together still and see each other in these different journeys of our life.”

#794. Record crowds, legends - Bordeaux bid to escape amateur game

Bordeaux fans protested when the club were demoted to the sixth tier

The latest stop on Zinedine Zidane's homecoming tour was an important one for the new France head coach. When Les Bleus took on Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday night, the ex-midfielder was returning to the city in which he spent four formative years of his playing career, between 1992 and 1996.

"I became a man in Bordeaux," Zidane fondly recalled in the build-up. France edged triumphed 2-1 with an uninspiring display, but it did not dampen the mood of the 40,000 fans inside the Stade Atlantique.

While the 1998 World Cup winner was not necessarily in familiar surroundings (the out-of-town stadium was built for Euro 2016, 20 years after his departure for Juventus), locals made every effort to make him feel at home, holding up a commemorative tifo before kick-off and chanting Zizou's name throughout.

Just a few miles up the road earlier that afternoon, Zidane's former club were playing their fifth match of the season in the sixth-tier Regional 1, in a north-western suburb of the city.

Thousands of Bordeaux fans had made the short away outing to Saint-Medard-en-Jalles' 3000-seater ground to watch their team seal a fifth win in five this season.

Girondins de Bordeaux, the six-time French champions, who were once regulars in European cups, now find themselves facing amateur opposition on a weekly basis.

Since 2022, the club has plummeted from Ligue 1 to the sixth tier through a combination of on-pitch struggles, mismanagement at all levels, and sanctions due to their financial troubles.

Listen to the latest Football Daily podcast

The club was taken over in 2021 by Gerard Lopez, who was previously in charge of Formula 1's Lotus as well as another French side, Lille.

While Bordeaux were already hamstrung by debts at that point, the situation on and off the pitch worsened under the Spanish-Luxembourgish businessman as the men's first team finished rock bottom of Ligue 1 in his first season.

A couple of seasons in Ligue 2 followed, before the club was docked down to the fourth tier in 2024. In their first National 2 season, they notably signed Andy Carroll but ultimately missed out on promotion.

The following campaign saw a repeat of that near miss, and the club was expelled from national-level football altogether this summer over their finances.

With Bordeaux left on the brink and whittled down to just eight full-time employees (down from around 250 a few years beforehand), Lopez sold up to Park Bench, a group of mainly British USA-based investors who also own Scottish side Dunfermline as well as a minority stake in Spanish second tier side Cordoba.

The supporters turned out in their numbers for the first home match of the campaign, which had been delayed amid the uncertainty over whether the club could continue running, against Stade Montois.

More than 11,000 tickets sold, a record crowd for that level of French football.

"140 years of history, we won't be stopped," read one of the banners held up by the Ultramarines fan group, who also made it a point to thank the seven first-team players who had stayed despite the club's double relegation.

The team is centred around a core of players with Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 experience. Steve Shamal, who scored a hat-trick in that 4-1 victory over Stade Montois, previously turned out for the likes of Caen and Annecy in the second tier.

"We know we should be higher up, but that certainty can also be a trap," said Shamal after the game. "We shouldn't think that it's going to be easy.

"We need to respect our opponents if we're going to put in good performances."

As the sixth tier of French football is regionalised, only the league winner in the Nouvelle Aquitaine region's top flight will earn promotion.

Their on-pitch success so far this season comes as little surprise given the gulf in quality compared to the rest of the league. Over the summer, Bordeaux notably managed to hold on to Europa League-winning full-back Almamy Toure, while former Belgian youth international striker Baptiste Guillaume also joined.

Several former players have also looked to get involved in Bordeaux's revival.

Benoit Tremoulinas, the former French international who was a part of the title-winning squad in 2008-09, notably announced that at the age of 40 he would be lacing up his boots again seven years after injury forced him to retire.

Paul Baysse, the former centre-back, is an assistant to head coach Arnaud Cormier.

Benoit Tremoulinas spent six years at Bordeaux, winning a league title and two cups, before also twice winning the Europa League with Sevilla

Perhaps the most significant endorsement the new owners could have hoped for was that of Alain Giresse, widely regarded as the club's greatest player. The Euro 1984 winner, who won three league titles while playing more than 500 times for the Marine et Blanc, was in attendance for the match against Stade Montois. He took the ceremonial kick-off before giving a full-time dressing room speech.

The new management unveiled their long-term plans for the club on Monday at Le Haillan, the city-owned training ground which includes a chateau that hosts the club's headquarters.

"We are humbled to have this responsibility," Park Bench investor Jeremy Green said.

"The club doesn't belong to Park Bench, it belongs to Bordeaux, it belongs to the 11,000 people who came to watch a Regional 1 game, to the players and to the community. We have a responsibility to rebuild this club.

"Our commitment to the community and to the players is that we will be fiscally responsible and patient.

"We're not a financial institution, we're a collection of individuals who bring with them business, sporting, analytical, and entrepreneurship skills."

Dominique Delport, the club's new president, revealed he knew Green and Twining through his wife, who studied at Oxford with them.

"We can learn from the club's golden years," the former journalist and advertising executive told BBC Sport, before adding that he would look to bring club legends to every league game.

Bordeaux won the Coupe de France as recently as 2013

While the club was sold for a symbolic euro, it did involve taking on long-standing debts which spanned transfer fees, stadium rent, and a compensation claim by former head coach Vladimir Petkovic.

Last Friday, the city's commercial court approved a request to restructure the debt as part of the club's continuation plan.

When Bordeaux were expelled from national-level football by the French FA at the start of the summer, the club used several avenues to appeal while the takeover was being finalised.

"We thought we had acquired the club in National 1 [the fourth tier]," Green and co-investor James Twining, told BBC Sport.

"Initially we walked away, but we were encouraged to come back," Green added. "We established that we were going to be able to restructure things and make it work.

"People around the club and in the local community encouraged us to try to find a way."

The six-time French champions have a long way to go before returning to the top flight.

"We're committing to a sensible financial structure, to a well-run club, and we're talking about 10 years to get this club back to Ligue 1," the new investors added.

A crucial step towards that long-term goal will be returning to the professional leagues, which would allow them to re-open the youth academy they were made to close when they dropped down.

Rebuilding the women's team, who were involved in the Champions League only a few seasons ago, is another one of the new owners' objectives.

Keeping the fans onside throughout the process will also be key, not least after the rift that opened up between groups during the previous ownership.

In any case, if the record-breaking turnout for Bordeaux's return to league action is anything to go by, their support seems unlikely to waver anytime soon.
