#792. Rob Kardashian Restores Cousin’s Vintage Car in Rare TV Appearance

While Rob Kardashian is mostly absent from his family’s Hulu series The Kardashians, his recent camo on a Prime Video series has a sweet nod to dad Robert Kardashian Sr.’s family.

Rob Kardashian is kicking his latest rare reality TV appearance into gear.

While his sisters are fixture of pop culture with their Hulu series The Kardashians, Rob has managed to stay mostly out of the spotlight in recent years. However, he made a rare exception for the latest episode of Fully Torqued Unleashed.

In the third episode of season three of the Prime Video series, which dropped Nov. 7, Rob makes a brief cameo to ask host Steve Pazamy to assist in a surprise for his father Robert Kardashian Sr.’s cousin Cici Bussey. The 39-year-old expressed that he wants to fix up Cici’s 1963 Mercedes, which she has owned over 20 years.

Later, Cici is floored by the gift and expressed her gratitude on camera.

“If it wasn’t for Rob, I wouldn’t have met Steve,” she said in an interview. “And if it wasn’t for Steve, my car wouldn’t look beautiful.”

But while Rob was willing to put himself on camera for the sake of his cousin once removed—as well as to celebrate his sister Kim’s 46th birthday last month—he has previously shared why he prefers to keep to himself.

“It just has everything to do with myself,” he told his sister Khloe Kardashian during a 2025 episode of Khloe in Wonder Land, emphasizing he remains tight with Khloe, as well as Kourtney Kardashian, Kim Kardashian and mom Kris Jenner, “There's definitely nothing wrong between any of us.”

For Rob—dad to daughter Dream, 10, with ex Blac Chyna—he simply doesn’t want to put himself in a situation where he’s not “comfortable.”

“Like, I'm not comfortable in my skin, so why would I wanna go be on camera and just be vulnerable and let people in?” the Arthur George founder continued. “That’s not what I wanna do.”

However, there is one part of filming that Rob does enjoy—enough to even bring him back from time to time.

“I love filming if it's positive and if it's natural and I'm feeling good about myself,” he expressed. “I like being around my family, so that stuff is good to me.”

Nevertheless, he admitted, “The reason I don't is because I'm a homebody and I just choose, like I said, my peace and happiness.”

For some of the Kardashians’ best TV moments over the years, keep reading…

Who can forget the time Khloe Kardashian was on her way to jail, and Kim Kardashian couldn't stop taking selfies. "Kim, would you stop taking pictures of yourself? Your sister's going to jail," Kris Jenner famously said.

When Khloe needed to get her ladyparts waxed for then-husband Lamar Odom, there was only one woman for the job—Kourtney Kardashian. Doesn't get more ride or die than that.

This was the episode where the world learned exactly what happens when you're rude to Kim. Kim hit Khloe with her handbag over and over again while saying, "Don't be f--king rude!" Lesson learned.

We died laughing when Khloe wouldn't let Kris in the car and Kris couldn't hold it any longer! When you gotta go, you gotta go.

The girls go to a winery in Napa, and Kris has a little to much to drink. While Kourtney and Khloe are sitting in the car Facetiming with French Montana, Kris greets him with a, "Hello, mother f--ker!"

Yes, there is a meaning behind Scott Disick's social media handle. Back in 2012, Kourtney's now-ex was officially dubbed a Lord and became London royalty right before our eyes.

Nothing was funnier than watching Kourtney struggle to have a conversation with Khloe while her mouth was completely numb from her trip to the dentist.

Scott had been known to pull a few pranks in his day, but the time he prank called Kris pretending to be Todd Kraines was legendary. "Auntie Kris, it's me! It's Todd Kraines!" will go down in history as our favorite quote ever.

In perhaps the most quotable Kardashian moment, Kim crying over her lost diamond earring was tragic, but Kourtney was there to add a little perspective: "Kim, there's people that are dying."

When Kris gifted Kylie this sweet baby pig back in 2016, the youngest Kardashian-Jenner memorably mistook it for the farm animal she really wanted. "Is that a chicken?" she shrieked once the housewarming present was unveiled. Upon closer examination, she realized her error.

#791. Former Spain midfielder Mata retires aged 38

Mata celebrates winning Euro 2012 with Spain

Former Spain midfielder Juan Mata has announced his retirement from playing at the age of 38.

Mata, who made 41 international appearances, was part of the Spain squad that won the 2010 World Cup, and he helped his country win the European Championship two years later when he scored in the 4-0 final victory against Italy.

A former Real Madrid youth player, he joined Valencia in 2007 before a move to Chelsea in August 2011 where he won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup.

Mata moved to Manchester United in January 2014 and helped them claim the Europa League, FA Cup and League Cup prior to his departure in 2022.

He went on to have spells at Turkish side Galatasaray and Vissel Kobe in Japan before he played for Australian sides Western Sydney Wanderers and Melbourne Victory.

"Football will never leave my life," said Mata. "There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development.

"I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer."

Mata was Chelsea's player of the year in both full seasons he was at Stamford Bridge. He made 82 league appearances for the club, scoring 18 goals.

"What a player," Chelsea posted on social media.

At Manchester United, he scored 51 goals in 285 outings before leaving after his contract expired.

"Congratulations on a fantastic career, Juan! Everyone at United wishes you all the best in your next steps," said United statement., external

#790. Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

#789. Leicester split with sponsor after porn actress row

BC Game has been the main shirt sponsor of Leicester City for two-and-a-half years

Leicester City have parted ways with their main shirt sponsor after the gambling firm appointed a porn actress as an ambassador.

BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the League One side at the start of the 2024-25 season - named Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month.

The online gambling company posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin."

The club, which had faced criticism from fans' group The Foxes Trust, said it had reached a "mutual agreement" to ends its partnership with the firm and fans who had bought shirts in the past 28 days could exchange them.

BC Game announced its new ambassador at the beginning of the month, prompting the trust to state: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people.

"Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?"

On Wednesday the club issued a statement which said it and the sponsor had "reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect".

It also thanked the firm for the "constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement".

The statement confirmed an "enhanced returns policy" where it would accept BC Game branded shirts bought since 21 October for exchange or refund even if they had been worn or personalised.

#788. Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?

The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

For members of the Indigenous Sasak community on the Indonesian island of Lombok, the conflict over their land is not over.

For them, a tourism and infrastructure project co-financed by the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is a source of frustration, as they believe it has led to the expropriation of their land and destruction of their livelihoods.

In late September, they officially filed a complaint with the bank. It remains unclear whether this complaint will lead to an independent investigation.

The AIIB, which finances major infrastructure projects across Asia, has a mechanism in place to deal with such complaints.

Individuals who suffer adverse effects from the bank-financed projects may, under certain conditions, file a complaint with the institution.

However, access to this process — known as the Project Complaints Mechanism (PPM) — remains controversial.

According to a report by The Diplomat, a magazine that covers political and economic developments in Asia, none of the 45 complaints listed on the AIIB's website had been deemed admissible as of mid-September.

The bank acknowledged that "no cases have passed the PPM's eligibility assessment," but it stressed that this is "only part of the story."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The AIIB emphasized that not every issue needs to be resolved through this mechanism.

The PPM is "only one part of AIIB's grievance redress ecosystem," the Beijing-based bank said in response to a query from DW.

Those affected should first attempt to resolve concerns directly with the project team at the local level, it said.

According to the bank, "twelve complaints were in fact resolved at the project level — as a direct result of AIIB's follow-up and intervention — and one was resolved through domestic courts."

But critics see this as a major weakness.

"The mechanism must be easily accessible," said Arntraud Hartmann, a development economist at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS Europe) in Bologna, Italy.

She argued that people affected by the projects, for instance, are required to document potential violations of environmental and social standards from the start. "How is the affected party supposed to know which standards might have been violated?" she questioned.

The AIIB disputes this claim. "In terms of accessibility, we have made the submission form simpler and translated it into 12 languages," it said, adding that complaints can be submitted online, by phone, or by email.

Urgewald, a German environmental NGO, cites another problem with AIIB-financed projects. For many of them, information on environmental impacts and resettlements is either missing or published late, it noted.

For 2024, the NGO found that 11 of the 16 projects it examined lacked complete environmental and social impact assessments. In many cases, information on the potential number of displaced residents was also missing, it added.

"The information published on the bank's website is often insufficient and inconsistent. Particularly important documents, such as environmental impact assessments or resettlement plans, vary widely or are missing entirely," said Nora Sausmikat, a China expert at Urgewald.

The lack of information makes it difficult for those affected to respond promptly and report violations early on, she underscored, adding that the situation is particularly difficult for people without formal land titles.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Christoph Steinert, a political scientist at the University of Konstanz, said the mere existence of such grievance redressal mechanisms "is not enough."

Particularly vulnerable groups often know little about their rights, he said, adding that information should be available in local languages and targeted outreach directed at affected communities.

Criticism of the AIIB's procedures is not new. A 2023 report by international aid organizations, including Recourse, Accountability Counsel, and Inclusive Development International, revealed that the AIIB's grievance mechanism had failed to accept a single complaint since its 2019 inception.

The study highlighted that 101 of the 219 AIIB-financed projects, or 46% of the total projects at the time, were ineligible for review due to co-financing exemptions.

The AIIB typically provides funding without leading projects, a standard practice in development finance. When complaints arise, it directs complainants to the lead lender. As a result, nine of the 45 complaints fell outside its jurisdiction.

For Sausmikat, this is part of the problem. "The AIIB, however, decided against revising this requirement and established a mechanism that is very difficult to access," she said.

As of January 1, 2026, following two years of external consultations, the AIIB reformed its complaints mechanism. Under certain conditions, complaints can now be filed even while legal proceedings are ongoing.

But Sausmikat stressed that the changes are insufficient. Of the eight key recommendations made by an independent expert, only three were adopted, she underlined. "The revision did not remove the actual obstacles."

The AIIB stated that the reforms are intended to make the mechanism "more accessible and responsive."

The new rules have been in effect for only 10 months, and their implementation is being closely monitored, the bank said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Steinert said fear of reprisals poses another fundamental challenge to such procedures.

Documented cases from Latin America, for instance, show that complainants have faced administrative or legal problems, and in some cases even violence.

Such risks could deter others from filing complaints, Steinert said.  However, his research does not specifically address AIIB projects.

The bank said that it "does not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises concerns."

"Requestors may ask for confidentiality, and the revised PPM policy strengthens protection against reprisals," it added.

Sausmikat said Germany — as a co-founder and the fourth-largest shareholder of the AIIB — could also play a role, working with other member states to push for changes.

Hartmann also stressed that the bank's shareholders bear responsibility and urged the AIIB's Board of Directors to amend the rules governing the grievance mechanism. "We need a policy based on good-practice standards."

This article was originally written in German.

#785. Strasbourg appoint Swansea boss Matos

Vitor Matos was under contract at Swansea until 2030

Strasbourg have announced the appointment of Swansea City's Vitor Matos as the club's new head coach.

The French top-flight side made the announcement on Wednesday evening, but there has been no official confirmation of Matos' departure from the Swans.

Strasbourg are expected to pay Swansea compensation thought to be in the region of Â£5m in order to secure his services.

Matos, 38, spent just under a year at Swansea having left his role at Maritimo to succeed Alan Sheehan as the Championship club's head coach in November 2025.

Four members of Matos' coaching team - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira - are also expected to leave Swansea.

Ex-captain Ashley Williams is set to return to the club to join an interim coaching team also featuring fellow former players Kristian O'Leary and Leon Britton.

O'Leary and Britton are set to be the only remaining members of Matos' Swansea staff.

Alongside Williams, they will lead Swansea while the club searches for Matos' permanent successor.

Their first game will be at home to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

Swansea go to Middlesbrough next Tuesday before hosting rivals Cardiff City on Sunday, 29 November.

Matos moves on despite agreeing an extended Swansea contract running until 2030 in July.

Leon Britton (left) and Ashley Williams (right) were Swansea team-mates in League One, the Championship and the Premier League

Swansea were 20th in the second tier when the former Liverpool coach took over, but he leaves a team lying only three points off the top of the table in sixth.

Matos led Swansea to an 11th-placed finish last season, and has raised hopes of a potential promotion push in 2026-27 thanks to an encouraging start to this campaign.

But he told Swansea he wanted to move on after Strasbourg, who have the same ownership group as Premier League side Chelsea, made their move last weekend and he said goodbye to players and staff on Tuesday.

Having finished eighth last season, Strasbourg are 13th in Ligue 1 having won only three of their 10 league games under Hugo Oliveira, who was only appointed in the summer after Gary O'Neil departed to take over at Ipswich Town.

Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views

Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he had also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact at Swansea.

When asked in October about the Palace links, Matos said: "I'm Swansea manager. I love being here, love my players, love the staff, so my focus is always on the next game and what we can do better."

In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs.

But Gorringe played down the idea of Matos being lured away, saying: "The reality is there'll always be interest in anyone performing well in any role on and off the pitch.

"That's one of the outcomes of being successful - we're aware of that.

"[But] we're all quite happy. We've all agreed to go on this journey together and we hope that Vitor is here a long time."

#782. Ella Langley Becomes First Act to Earn Top Two of TouchTunes Frontline Chart

"Choosin' Texas" was the most-played song of the third quarter of 2026 on TouchTunes jukeboxes, while Langley's "Be Her" is No. 2 on the Frontline list.

For the first time since the inception of the TouchTunes Frontline and Catalog charts in 2024, the same artist occupies the top two positions of either ranking.

Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” remains at No. 1 on the Frontline Chart for the third quarter of 2026, and Langley’s “Be Her” zooms to No. 2. Related Noah Kahan Reacts to 2027 Grammy Nominations Snub: 'I Was In My Feelings for a Sec' 'Grand Theft Auto VI' Revs Its Engines & Leads 2026 Game Awards Nominations: Full List Cody Johnson on Why He's Skipping 2026 CMA Awards: 'Going 100 MPH All the Time Isn't Healthy' Explore Ella Langley See latest videos, charts and news

The TouchTunes charts for the third quarter of 2026 track the most played songs and artists on TouchTunes jukeboxes from July 1 to Sept. 30, 2026, with the Frontline ranking inclusive of music released in the last 18 months, followed by the Catalog tally for any music that was released more than 18 months ago. The TouchTunes Artists Chart tracks the same period, combining an artist’s plays across both rankings. TouchTunes has jukeboxes in more than 60,000 locations worldwide. Its data is not factored into other Billboard charts.

“Choosin’ Texas” has spent the entirety of 2026 at No. 1 on the Frontline Chart, after debuting at No. 2 for the fourth quarter of 2025. But while the rankings have seen similarly dominant leaders — think Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” and, on Catalog, Chris Stapleton’s “Tennessee Whiskey” — Q3 of 2026 marks the first time one of those acts was able to occupy the entire top two of one of the tallies, with “Be Her” up to No. 2 on Frontline after reaching No. 3 in the second quarter of the year.

In all, Langley is featured on the Frontline survey five times, four as a lead act (her Morgan Wallen duet “I Can’t Love You Anymore” at No. 11 and “Dandelion” at No. 23) and once as the featured performer on BigXthaPlug’s “Hell at Night” at No. 6. She also appears on Catalog at No. 7 via “You Look Like You Love Me,” a duet with Riley Green. Combined, that puts her at No. 2 on the TouchTunes Artists Chart for another quarter, behind perennial No. 1 Wallen.

Following Langley, there’s quite the turnover on Frontline for the latest quarter, with nine debuts among the 25-position chart. Yung Miami’s “Spend Dat” leads the pack at No. 3, followed by Stella Lefty’s “Boston” at No. 4.

“Tennessee Whiskey” remains top dog on Catalog, with Toby Keith’s “I Love This Bar” rising to No. 2. The chart features a top-10 debut in Wallen’s “I’m the Problem,” which bows at No. 8 after graduating to Catalog from Frontline, where it had been No. 2 for Q2.

The August death of Dolly Parton drives a pair of the country legend’s songs onto Catalog in “Jolene” at No. 6 and “9 to 5” at No. 15, while Parton herself bows at No. 7 on the Artists Chart.

Yet again, it’s rock that leads the overall genre ranking for catalog titles, accounting for 37% of plays in the third quarter, down 3% from the second. Country leads frontline-specific songs with 43% of all plays.

See all three charts below. The rankings will continue with the fourth quarter of 2026 (Oct. 1-Dec. 31, 2026), which will include National Jukebox Day on Nov. 25; TouchTunes is currently soliciting examples of hometown songs for its Hometown Jukebox Anthems initiative for the 2026 date.

#781. Manchester won't always be blue - Pochettino

The longest commute for a first day on the job?

Mauricio Pochettino says there is no time to waste as he sets out to restore Manchester United to being the city's most successful club.

The Argentine arrived to begin his new role as United manager on Wednesday after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract.

The USA beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati in his final game in charge on Tuesday, after which he spoke to TNT Sports., external

Analyst DaMarcus Beasley, who spent the 2006-07 season on loan with Manchester City, joked that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue".

Pochettino replied: "No way, you will see. Give me time and that is going to change."

The former Chelsea, Tottenham and Southampton boss flew directly to Manchester on a private jet after the game and landed at about 11:30 GMT before heading to the club's Carrington training ground.

Pochettino's first game in charge is on Sunday, when United travel to face rivals Liverpool at Anfield (16:30 GMT).

"I have plenty of energy. It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United. And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday," he said in his first interview to the club's in-house media team.

"Now it's not time to think about rest, it's not time to think about sleep.

"It's about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield."

United are currently 18th in the Premier League having won just once this term, with Liverpool 14 places and 10 points above them.

"We know that it is not a situation that deserves to be at a club like Manchester United and for the fanbase," Pochettino added.

"We're excited because the new challenge is big, but it's the adrenaline that you want to feel," he said.

"We are going to have a different job but we have the experience to deal with that. We need to add our common sense in the way that we are going to approach all the things."

Tuesday's win ensured the US advanced to the Concacaf Nations League semi-finals and that Pochettino finished with a 62.16% win ratio from 37 games in charge.

Mauricio Pochettino became head coach of the USA men's national team in September 2024

The 54-year-old led the team to the 2025 Gold Cup final and the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup, when the US were co-hosts.

"I am proud of what we achieved," Pochettino said in a statement on Instagram., external

"When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team.

"This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally.

"Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

"I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves."

#780. Jenny McCarthy’s Son Evan Asher Tearfully Vows to Buy Back Family Home

Jenny McCarthy’s son Evan Asher broke down in tears while sharing the “saddest moment” of his life, moving out of his mom and stepdad Donnie Wahlberg’s home, noting he hopes to "one day" buy it back.

Jenny McCarthy’s son Evan Asher isn’t masking his feelings about leaving his childhood home.

Over a month after the Masked Singer judge confirmed she and her husband Donnie Wahlberg were moving from St. Charles, Ill. to Las Vegas, her 24-year-old son shared an emotional video, in which he tearfully expressed his sadness over saying goodbye to his childhood home.

“The saddest moment of my entire life has hit me harder than ever,” Asher, who was diagnosed with autism around age 3, wrote in a Nov. 15 Instagram post, which featured a video of him crying in the car. “I have officially moved away from my home and life just won’t be the same anymore. And I’m so sorry I was very emotional.”

“But when you live somewhere most of your life, have so many friends, and make more nostalgic memories than everything in any other house that you’ve lived in it’s a lot to take in,” the content creator continued. “So I knew I had to share my emotions with you all.”

While Asher—whom McCarthy shares with ex John Asher—navigates the difficult goodbye, he voiced his hope that the new owners will have an impactful experience as he did. That said, the YouTuber did reveal he plans to return to the Chicago-area home someday.

“One day. ONE DAY. I will buy this place again and start a family of my own,” he promised, adding, “Thank you house for everything overall. I love you and god bless you.”

And Asher didn’t hold back in sharing his emotions with his followers, breaking down in tears as he filmed himself riding in a car.

As he admitted, “It just really hurts. It hurts really bad. I’m just not doing great.”

In late September, McCarthy and Wahlberg listed their Tudor-style home, with the Two and a Half Men alum revealing in the comments of a People Sept. 24 Instagram post that the family was “going to Vegas. Not Cali.”

While the couple has yet to open up about the reason behind the move, McCarthy shared earlier this year that she was having “constant infections” due to the mold in her home, sharing that she was “living in a tent” at one point.

It’s no surprise the couple are looking to make Vegas their permanent home. Wahlberg—dad to sons Xavier, 33, and Elijah, 25, with ex-wife Kim Fey—has been hitting the stage with New Kids on the Block for the past year and a half for their Vegas residency. Plus, his younger brother Mark Wahlberg and his family also live in the city.

Despite his emotional reaction to the move, Asher emphasized that his mom and stepdad “made the right decision.”

And McCarthy proved that she supports his decision to buy the home when he gets older.

“Promise someday you’re gonna knock on that door and buy it for your family,” she commented on his Instagram video. “It’s not goodbye. It’s see you later. I love you. Hugging and kissing your heart.”

#779. The 3pm football blackout: Outdated or still relevant in 2026?

The 3pm blackout has existed in English football since the 1960s

After 60 years, is time finally running out on the 3pm blackout in football?

With pretty much every available television slot now exhausted, next year the Premier League and the EFL are set to hold serious discussions about its future.

There are concerns, especially within non-league football, that removing the blackout could have detrimental effects on attendances and finances.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham agrees, urging caution and suggesting the health of the football pyramid should come first.

But many Premier League fans feel they are short-changed, locked out of many of their team's fixtures just because they live in this country.

Go anywhere else in the world, and every single match is available live.

With streaming so prevalent, to some the blackout feels archaic.

Yet it is a complex situation, and many feel the depth of English football's pyramid is like nowhere else.

BBC Sport looks at the history of the blackout, why it is unique to British football and the arguments for and against keeping it.

It is the start of the 1964-65 season and the BBC launches a programme called Match of the Day.

Highlights of one match would be broadcast on BBC Two, a channel which at the time was only available in London.

Yet some clubs were concerned. Would fans still turn up to games?

Burnley chairman Bob Lord was the first owner to refuse to allow the cameras into Turf Moor. At the end of the season, several other clubs tried to block the renewal of the deal.

A compromise was reached and the BBC agreed not to reveal the televised Saturday match until all games had ended.

Shortly afterwards came the blackout for live matches.

Fast forward 20 years to 1987. With dwindling attendances across the European domestic leagues, partly influenced by crowd trouble, Uefa took up England's idea.

Article 48 was added to the Uefa Statutes.

Each country could designate a two-and-a-half-hour "transmission-free period", as long as at least 50% of matches in the top two leagues were taking place.

This was "designed to ensure that spectators are not deterred from attending local football matches of any kind and/or participating in matches at amateur and/or youth level".

Today, the situation has gone full circle. The only leagues that apply Article 48 are England, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

The reason for this is simpler than you might imagine.

No other major country qualifies for the blackout - because no other major country has a kick-off time that runs from the top flight and through the divisions.

It is a tradition that is unique to football in the United Kingdom.

Let's take Germany, often held up as an example of a country with excellent attendances despite not having a blackout.

This misses a key point. The Bundesliga has its own kick-off slot, 3:30pm on a Saturday, and no other division plays at the same time. The 2. Bundesliga, for instance, has a standard Saturday kick-off time of 1:30pm.

Could you imagine English football replicating this?

In Spain, it is rare for either of the top two divisions to have games that kick off simultaneously. Each match has its own slot, and is broadcast live.

In Italy, Serie A plays on a Sunday afternoon, and Serie B on a Saturday.

In France, Ligue 1 has Saturday night as its main time slot, Ligue 2 plays largely on a Friday night, and Ligue 3 on a Saturday lunchtime.

So there is no blackout, because the football calendar works in a completely different way.

Football fans give their thoughts on the Saturday 3pm TV blackout

The next television rights cycle presents a unique opportunity.

The deals for the Premier League, EFL and Scottish Premiership are all up for renewal in 2029-30.

There is the chance for all the top stakeholders to come together and agree to end the blackout.

Last year, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said there were no plans to remove the blackout.

But this summer there was a clear shift in emphasis, with Masters admitting there would be talks with the EFL ahead of the renewal of TV rights.

Scottish football has gone first, with broadcasters invited to bid to show all matches live - and is open to those shown on a Saturday afternoon.

It will be another year before we discover what the Premier League and the EFL - which seriously considered ending the blackout three years ago - are prepared to offer to broadcasters.

So, why would the leagues need to offer up the Saturday 3pm slot to broadcasters? After all, the latest domestic Premier League deal was worth a record Â£6.7bn - an increase of 4%.

However, to achieve that figure, the Premier League had to make an additional 70 games available. In real terms, it means each live Premier League game is worth less than it was before.

Now every single game not shown at 3pm on a Saturday - and there are only 110 left - is on TV.

Could the Premier League need to offer more matches for the rights to keep their overall value?

If so there are two options: try to find more TV slots, or show games at 3pm on a Saturday.

Could the Women's Super League benefit too? It looked into playing a 3pm on a Saturday but could not find a way around the blackout.

Most of the competition's games are shown live already, with a greater concern being stadium availability and consistency of kick-off times.

There is a danger that the issue of the 3pm blackout is viewed only through the lens of Premier League and EFL television rights.

Tom Greatrex, the chair of the Football Supporters' Association, says there are attendances in non-league football that some top flights in Europe "would look at jealously".

"We have one of the strongest football pyramids in the world, with excellent matchday attendances deep into the non-league game," Greatrex said.

"The prime minister is right to point out the value of the blackout to clubs further down the pyramid, and to urge caution over the impact rushed change could have on the overall health of the game."

BBC Sport understands that senior executives at the National League, which has a long-term global streaming deal with DAZN, are steadfastly against the blackout ending.

It has serious reservations, shared by the vast majority of its 72 clubs, that attendances would be impacted.

Included in this is transient attendance from season ticket holders of league clubs, many of whom go to non-league football when their team is away from home, boosting receipts considerably.

The fear is this could be lost if all league games are streamed at 3pm.

Nick Boom, the chair of Northern Premier League side FC United of Manchester, worries that the issue is only viewed through the lens of top-flight football.

"Football doesn't begin and end with the Premier League," Boom told BBC Sport.

"Every Saturday, thousands of people turn out to support their local clubs.

"For many of those clubs, the income from people coming through the turnstiles, buying a pint or something to eat is what keeps them alive.

"The 3pm blackout isn't about nostalgia. It's about protecting something that matters."

Boom added that clubs in non-league football are huge community assets, and losing them would have an impact "well beyond 90 minutes on a Saturday".

Some clubs are more open-minded about what ending the blackout could mean for non-league football.

Others have changed the way they operate to get around it.

North West Counties League Premier Division side FC Isle of Man have stopped playing at 3:00pm on a Saturday so they can stream all their games live.

Brian Shotton, a director at eighth-tier Ashington FC, told BBC Sport that he would not be automatically against removing the blackout.

"I would still have concerns, because every person through the gate makes a difference," Shotton said.

"I don't think we should just assume it would damage non-league football, but equally you need to know what it could mean for clubs like ours."

Ashington, who have attendances of about 400, see gates rise by up to 25% when Newcastle are not at home - but they already feel the impact of illegal streaming of the Magpies' games.

For the official broadcasters like Sky Sports, these supporters are seen as lost revenue.

There is an argument that the blackout drives piracy. Just how many of those particular fans would pay for a legal subscription is open to debate.

Added to that, there are now many weekends when fewer than 50% of matches in the top two divisions are played at 3pm on a Saturday anyway.

For instance, on 28 November there are just two in the Premier League, and seven in the Championship.

Other non-league clubs, like Dorking Wanders and Hashtag United, have spoken of the opportunities ending the blackout could bring, such as more income streams and fewer inconvenient kick-off times.

But this, for now, seems to be a minority view. The concerns for the health of the entire pyramid, on attendances and finances, are real.

Once the blackout is gone, it is unlikely to come back.

#778. Democracy study: One-quarter of Germans want a right-wing authoritarian dictatorship

The far-right AfD's electoral successes point to a new trend in Germany: Prejudice, resentment, and extremism are on the rise. A new study suggests satisfaction with democracy is at a low ebb.

Satisfaction with democracy in Germany has hit a new low, while the past is being idealized, and people are expressing a longing for a radical break. Antisemitic sentiments and the desire for an authoritarian leader are also on the rise. These are key findings of the authoritarianism study presented Wednesday in Berlin, which has been conducted every two years since 2002.

The study, led by the Else Frenkel-Brunswik Institute for Democracy Research at the University of Leipzig, is based on the answers to a questionnaire by 2,507 respondents, who the researchers say are a representative cross-section of the German population.

For the first time since the study series began, approval of democracy as an idea fell just below the 90% mark, which the study said is primarily attributable to a loss of trust among respondents in the former East Germany (85.7%). The decline in approval of democracy as experienced in everyday life is even more severe: Nationwide, only one-third are satisfied with democracy, with figures having fallen sharply both in eastern (22.8%) and western (36%) states.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The growing rejection of democracy is also reflected in the desire for some kind of authoritarian nationalist government: Just under a quarter of respondents explicitly supported the idea of a "single strong party that embodies the national community as a whole." In the east, the figure stands at 30.9%, above the Germany-wide average of 22.3%.

"Our democracy is under great pressure. It has lost acceptance among the general population. It is alarming how much an authoritarian yearning is taking its place," concluded social psychologist and study author Oliver Decker.

Far-right attitudes have risen for the second consecutive year. Of particular note in the study was what the researchers called a chauvinistic national pride, which, with 19.9% approval, has reached its highest level since the study series began. The proportion of people with a consistently far-right worldview has reached 6.9%, the highest level since 2014, the study found.

Just under 15% of respondents said they explicitly believe that "everything has to fall apart so that something new can emerge," while nearly one in three respondents believes that "something radical is needed for the current state of affairs to change." Another 29.1% agree with this to some extent.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

According to the study, those who share this yearning for catastrophe exhibit significantly stronger antisemitic sentiments — and both are linked to a preference for certain political parties. The study found that a large proportion of eligible voters with this orientation favor the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD).

"Through its violent rhetoric, the AfD promises to realize the political goals of far-right ideology," the study said. The party's form and content, in other words, correspond exactly to the message that a significant portion of the population wants to hear. "It offers a political home to those who adhere to far-right thinking, while at the same time presenting itself as capable of connecting with a broad segment of society."

Study co-author Johannes Kiess calls on political leaders at all levels to find countermeasures. "The rejection of the present state of the world must be countered with compelling democratic alternatives and the ability to take political action today," he said. This also applies to the significant rise in antisemitism, which has more than doubled since 2022.

When asked about the motives behind antisemitic attitudes, the results show that for 16% of respondents, the policies of Israel's government are the decisive factor. This, too, is a record high in the context of the long-term study. While the figure in 2020 was significantly higher in the east (12%) than in the west (8.4%), the figures have since converged. Antisemitism related to Israel is actually slightly stronger in western than in eastern states.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Hostility toward Muslims is also on the rise. It peaked at over 40% in 2018, before dropping to well below 30%, and currently stands at 34.1%. These figures are based on two statements respondents were asked to agree with in each survey: "Muslims should be prohibited from immigrating to Germany" and "because of the many Muslims here, I sometimes feel like a stranger in my own country."

Misogyny is another issue regularly surveyed in the study. In the current survey, 18.3% agreed with anti-feminist statements. Notably, until now, a higher proportion of East Germans had been opposed to feminist causes. As recently as 2024, the difference between the former East (34.6%) and West (19.6%) was enormous. Two years later, the figure in the east has halved to 17.8%, while in western Germany it has fallen only slightly to 18.4%.

Despite the negative trend, there is a glimmer of hope at the end of the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study: While the results are "alarming," long-term trends show that a reversal of this trend is possible: "In earlier surveys, far-right statements already achieved high approval ratings, which then declined again in subsequent years. In addition to the influence of societal crises, political action and its societal perception are of central importance."

This article was originally written in German. It was first published on November 11 and later edited for clarity.

#777. Underscores Is First Transgender Woman Nominated for Best Dance/Electronic Recording Grammy

The 2027 nominations in this category are also significant for the number of women nominated.

The Grammys are making history this year, with first-time nominee Underscores now the first out transgender woman to be nominated for best dance/electronic recording. The artist got the nod for “Music,” from her March album U.

Many transgender women have paved the way for this accomplishment, with SOPHIE, Kim Petras, Arca, Honey Dijon, Wendy Carlos, Jackie Shane and Teddy Geiger all receiving nominations over the years. In 2023, Petras became the first transgender woman to win a Grammy, when she got the award for best pop duo/group performance for her Sam Smith collab “Unholy.”

In her acceptance speech, Petras acknowledged this achievement, saying, “I just want to thank all the incredible transgender legends before me who kicked these doors open for me so I could be here tonight. SOPHIE especially, my friend who passed away two years ago who told me this would happen and always believed in me… Madonna for fighting for LGBTQ rights. I don’t think I could be here without Madonna. My mother — I grew up next to a highway in nowhere Germany and my mother believed me that I was a girl, and I wouldn’t be here without her and her support.”

Trans women are also making history elsewhere at the 2027 Grammys, with Geese’s Emily Green being the first out trans woman nominated for best new artist, best rock performance, best alternative music performance, best alternative music album and best rock song.

The 2027 dance/electronic recording category is also significant for the number of woman nominated, with Madonna’s “I Feel So Free,” Slayyyter’s “Crank” and Tinashe’s “Melatonin” all nominated alongside Underscores and fellow nominees Fred again.. (for “Lights Burn Dimmer”) and Tame Impala (for “My Old Ways”).

This marks the first time four solo women acts were nominated for best dance/electronic recording since 2000, when the nominees were Gloria Estefan for “Don’t Let This Moment End,” Jennifer Lopez for “Waiting For Tonight,” Donna Summer for “I Will Go With You (Con te Partirò),” Fatboy Slim for “Praise You” and Cher for “Believe,” with this latter song winning the award.

#776. Kim Kardashian Reveals She Bought SKIMS Dupes From the TikTok Shop

Kim Kardashian confessed she is obsessed with buying items on the TikTok Shop, including dupes of her SKIMS products in order to “see how s--tty they are.”

Kim Kardashian is keeping up with the quality of products on the TikTok Shop.

After the SKIMS founder learned how to use Apple Pay, she confessed she’s putting it to good use as her “TikTok Shop bills are outrageous.”

The most surprising purchase she most recently made? Well, SKIMS dupes, of course.

“They have so many dupes,” Kardashian told Amanda Hirsch on the Nov. 17 episode of her Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast, “and I want to see how s--tty they are.”

As for her review of the wannabe SKIMS products, she doesn’t quite see the competition as up to par, revealing, “It didn't fit because it was like a bodysuit and the sizing was so off.”

But despite the low-quality dupe, Kardashian—who has her kids North, 13, Saint, 10, Chicago, 8, and Psalm, 7, to thank for setting up Apple Pay—has found herself obsessed with filling up her TikTok Shop cart.

“I buy everything,” the 46-year-old continued. “I am influenced. I buy lashes and I don’t even put on fake lashes myself. I buy every makeup because I want to know what’s out there. And they make it look so good.”

In fact, the Kardashians star is so in love with swiping through the virtual aisles, she created a new project around the hobby.

“I filmed this whole TikTok series [where] I was gonna test the products and give a real, honest answer, because sometimes a TikTok Shop product is such bulls--t,” she explained. “I have a whole list of things that are amazing but then I have a whole list of s--tty things.”

However, Kardashian’s candid reviews may not see the light of day because she admittedly “chickened out” on finishing the series. And now, the All’s Fair actress is left with a slight problem.

“I bought all these products. I’m not kidding you, I have a room full of hundreds of products,” she said. “I buy everything that probably exists on the TikTok Shop.”

Of course, Kardashian’s TikTok obsession is just the latest venture in her storied career. For a look back at her life through the years, keep reading…

#775. Ukrainian FA to blame for failed drugs test - Mudryk

Mudryk joined Chelsea in a deal worth up to Â£89m in January 2023

On-loan Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk says he blames the administration of the Ukraine national team for his failed drugs test and subsequent ban from football.

The 25-year-old, on a season-long loan from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, which he believes entered his system while on international duty.

Having initially faced a four-year ban from the Football Association (FA), his appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport was successful.

He returned to football after accepting he had breached anti-doping rules and agreeing to a suspension equivalent to the time he had already served.

After appearing for Chelsea during a pre-season tour of Asia, Mudryk joined Tottenham on transfer deadline day to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk manager Roberto de Zerbi.

In a lengthy interview with the Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk was asked who he blamed for his absence from the game.

"The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team," he replied. "It should never have existed. I probably haven't said it publicly yet, but I'm saying it now.

"I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England."

He explained how he had only been in Ukraine to be with the national team and "it points to the fact it was in a national team camp".

Asked specifically whether he blamed the national team, Mudryk replied: "Yes, exactly."

He also said Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF) president Andriy Shevchenko offered little support, blamed the association for leaks that emerged during the case and claimed its handling of the matter delayed his return to football.

Mudryk also said he spent millions of pounds on legal fees, coaching, pitch hire and private physiotherapy while being unable to access services at Chelsea.

He added: "It was a bolt from the blue. I couldn't believe it [the positive test] was true.

"It was like falling off a skyscraper. In a dream you would hit the ground. In life, I just kept on falling. It hit me very hard, mentally."

Mudryk said he cried and drank alcohol after the initial suspension but never doubted that he would eventually return to top-level football.

BBC Sport has contacted the UAF for comment.

Last year a UAF spokesperson told BBC Sport it was "in close contact with Mudryk's lawyers" but had not been contacted by the FA about the case.

#774. Florence Pugh Reacts to “Disturbing” Speculation About Her Appearance

Florence Pugh responded to online speculation that she had work done on her face: "I turned 30. I’m a woman...faces change.”

Florence Pugh isn’t worrying about the rumor mill, darling.

The East of Eden star responded to speculation that she’s had work done after fans theorized the reason for her newly chiseled jawline.

After a content creator said she thinks “that we can all collectively agree that Hollywood seems to have this thing against softer features,” with stars wanting “this sculpted, snatched look,” in a video shared to Evie Magazine’s Instagram Nov. 17, Pugh addressed why “her jaw is more sharp.”

As the Marvel star said of the side-by-side photos of herself in the video, “Guys. I turned 30. I’m a woman. [Bodies] and faces change.”

“It’s not that deep, the fact that people can’t even tell between what’s aging and what’s surgery is disturbing,” she added in the post’s comments section. “Sadly puppy fluff doesn’t last forever.”

She further addressed her shock over the matter in a vulnerable social media statement.

“I find it so stressful waking up and have thousands of people talking about you and your body in ways that you can’t even comprehend,” she wrote on Instagram Nov. 18. “I woke up the other morning and quite a lot of you were discussing my face and body in such a disturbing way.”

She noted, "I learnt online that I had been on ozempic? I learnt that I’d had upper bleph? Lower bleph? Filler? Face lipo? Bucal fat remover? Chin surgery? Nose surgery?!”

“I have spent my whole career defending and protecting bodies that just grow the way they grow,” she added. “I was subjected to fat shaming in the business from the moment I started and I have loved everytime I get to tell someone to f--k off when they are being inappropriate about my weight, and I’m not changing that now just because you’ve all said so.”

And just for the record, the Little Women actress wants fans to know she’s perfectly happy in the skin she’s in.

“I have never been on Ozempic,” she wrote. “I have NEVER done any face surgery. And don’t EVER say that I didn’t make my own nose, I’ve always had that beautiful ski slope. Even as a baby!”

Rather, Pugh credits any difference in her appearance to a lifestyle change.

“Here’s the truth, I turned 30 and my New Year’s resolution was to change my relationship with alcohol, and to be able to do at least one pull up in the gym,” she continued. “For the first time in my ENTIRE career, I have had the opportunity to be rested, to sleep, to wake up and work out and to eat regularly and healthily.”

And she won’t let internet fodder about her body throw her off her game.

“I’ve f--king worked so hard to clean my head and clean my body because I don’t want to allow space for negativity in my mind to grow,” she added. “I’m looking after myself, and that’s literally it.”

Keep reading for more stars who have set the record straight on getting cosmetic enhancements…

The Euphoria actress confirmed in December 2025 that she hasn't had a boob job.

As costar Amanda Seyfried told her during Vanity Fair's Lie Detector Test, “There’s been a question on everybody’s minds recently, and I just have to ask, are your boobs real?”

“Yes,” Sydney responded. “I’ve never gotten any work done anywhere.”

She shared in December 2025 that she's never gotten filler.

“As you are going along in your journey, I don’t think that you should overdo it with surgery, filler, Botox,” she told People. “You don’t need to do too much. Take it easy. Less is always better."

Travis Barker and ex Shanna Moakler's daughter has been open about her use of lip fillers but denies having cosmetic surgery.

In February 2024, she shared photos of herself wearing a bikini on Instagram, to which a user commented, "This child has done alot of cosmetic surgery @ a very young age, I hope she doesn't over do it! She looks good now!"

The rapper responded, "I really appreciate the love! I'm natural, besides my lips, accept the fact I'm naturally beautiful."

The Twilight alum told Harper's Bazaar U.K. in 2015 she will "never" get plastic surgery, adding, "I am so freaked out by the idea of doing anything. And maybe that's completely arrogant but I don't want to change anything about myself. I think the women who do are losing their minds. It's vandalism."

The Devil Wears Prada star told Good Housekeeping in 2008. "You have to embrace getting older. Life is precious, and when you've lost a lot of people, you realize each day is a gift."

The "God's Plan" rapper shut down rumors in September 2025 that he had plastic surgery to make his abs more defined, explaining the fan speculation was a result of using a photo editing app.

"I came from the gym, I was sweaty in that pic," he said during an episode of Bobbi Althoff’s Not This Again podcast. "Maybe I heightened the saturation or something on it."

He added, "I think I hit it too hard. They don't look like that."

While Drake noted that people go under the knife "all the time," he isn’t one of them.

"People also say that I got a BBL," he continued, referencing the popular Brazilian Butt Lift procedure. "They call me 'BBL Drizzy.'"

The supermodel opened up about why she's all about embracing her skin at every age.

"This is a 58 year old face without fillers, Botox or surgery in good light with professional gorgeous makeup," she wrote in an August 2023 Instagram caption. "I have chosen not to put anything 'into' my face."

She continued, "Some days, I like it. I feel like my face has gained character even as it's lost its youthful prettiness. And it seems a fair trade off."

The Oscar winner revealed whether or not she's gotten plastic surgery.

"My face is changing," she told Allure in an interview published August 2023, "and I love that my face is changing and aging. People think I had a facelift. They're like, 'What did she do to her face?' I'm like, 'Bitch, I'm just aging! It doesn't mean I got bad plastic surgery. This is just what happens.'"

The Pitch Perfect alum admitted she's never gotten any cosmetic injectables, telling People in 2023, "I've never put a needle in my face. And by the way, most people do it and truly, there's no judgement. But I make my living with my face."

She added, "Basically I'm terrified of f--king it up."

The Magic Mike actress set the record straight on whether or not she's gotten facial injectables. "No Botox!" she put it bluntly on Kelly Ripa's Let's Talk Off Camera podcast.

The "Summertime Sadness" singer denied having a surgical procedure on her nose after a fan referenced her "natural nose."

“Still never even been under the knife or anesthesia in my life for the 15th year in a row!!” Lana wrote on Instagram in September 2025, per a screenshot captured by People. “But if u use filler like [my doctor] used to- to build up the bridge of your nose it looks tall no bump. Takes seven minutes.”

The nonsurgical rhinoplasty Lana referred is “a cosmetic procedure where dermal fillers are used to temporarily change the shape of your nose,” according to the Cleveland Clinic. Though the procedure is less invasive, the results only last up to six months.

In 2021, the supermodel, who rose to fame in the '90s as one of the first, sued Zeltiq Aesthetics, alleging that its CoolScupting fat-reducing procedures that she underwent in 2015 and 2016 left her "permanently disfigured." The parties reached a settlement in the case in 2022.

In January 2021, while pregnant, the model wrote on her Instagram Story in response to fans' questions: "For anyone saying 'you need to stop w/ the lip injections': I've never had lip injections (no judging folks who do—ya'll look great!) but you can't even get injections when you're pregnant!"

Jenny from the Block continues to look like Jenny from the Block. In January 2021, she told an Instagram user, "I have never done Botox or any other injectables or surgery!! Just sayin'."

The Friends actress did have a nose job when she was younger to fix a deviated septum, but has spoke out against Botox and other facial fillers.

"There is also this pressure in Hollywood to be ageless," she told Yahoo! Beauty in 2014. "I think what I have been witness to, is seeing women trying to stay ageless with what they are doing to themselves. I am grateful to learn from their mistakes, because I am not injecting s--t into my face."

"I've probably tried everything. I would be scared to go under the knife, but you know, talk to me when I'm 50. I'll try anything. Except I won't do Botox again, because I looked crazy," the actress told Harper's Bazaar in 2013.

The Charlie's Angels alum told InStyle magazine in 2012, "I say, don't fight the rings on the trunk of a tree. Just keep counting 'em."

"The idea of not looking like myself scares me," she added.

The Love Actually actress told The Telegraph in 2011, "I'm not fiddling about with myself. We're in this awful youth-driven thing now where everybody needs to look 30 at 60."

"Nah. It's not my thing," the Oscar winner told MORE magazine in 2007. "I don't have anything against it for other people. Whatever they want to do, I'm fine with it. For me, it's really a self-image thing. Like, I'd rather have somebody go, "Wow, that girl has a big nose" than 'Wow, that girl has a bad nose job.' I'd rather have a comment about who I am than about something that identifies me as being ashamed of who I am."

In 2011, the pop star told Harper's Bazaar, "I think that promoting insecurity in the form of plastic surgery is infinitely more harmful than an artistic expression related to body modification."

In 2011, the Titanic star told the U.K. newspaper The Telegraph that cosmetic surgery goes against her morals, the way her parents brought her up and what she considers to be "natural beauty."

"I will never give in," she added. "I am an actress, I don't want to freeze the expression of my face."

#773. Why the integration of immigrants in Germany remains a challenge

The Federal Office for Migration and Refugees has released a new Integration Report. It found that while the integration of people with a migrant background is improving, violent youth remain a problem.

Few topics in Germany spark as many heated debates as integration. How successful have efforts been to integrate new arrivals? What is needed to enable successful integration? And what are the biggest problems?

Every two years, the government's Commissioner for Integration presents a comprehensive set of statistics on the matter. Since last year, that role has been held by Natalie Pawlik, a parliamentary representative from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD).

Speaking in Berlin on Wednesday, Pawlik offered an overall positive assessment: "Integration is improving steadily, despite ongoing hurdles and challenges." She continued: "The people of our country want integration to succeed. They rightly expect that people who live in Germany permanently will learn our language and abide by our laws."

The Commissioner for Integration is part of the Federal Ministry of Labor because ensuring that newcomers find work quickly is especially important.

The integration reportwas created by a team led by Frank Kalter, director of the German Center for Integration and Migration Research (DeZIM), drawing on official government statistics, surveys and independent studies. They found that when all immigrant groups are counted, about 30% of the population today has some sort of migration background — even if that comes down to only one parent.

Pawlik commented: "This is an important message at a time when the discussion often focuses primarily on problems related to supposedly failed integration." Kalter also pointed out that the employment rate among immigrants in Germany is higher than in most other EU countries — nearly 70%.

And they work primarily in one sector: "In recent years, the biggest increase of workers without German citizenship has been in the health and social services sector." According to the data, there were about 1.8 million people without a German passport working in Germany in 2009. By 2025, this number had more than tripled to 5.8 million.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

However, problems remain. In nearly all immigrant groups, women have difficulty finding employment, especially if they have children and their husbands are employed. Only about 60% of women in such families are employed, whereas nearly 88% of women in families with German passports are employed.

There are also immigrant groups that face barriers to accessing educational opportunities and the job market. These are mostly young men who came to Germany as refugees. And if one considers citizenship as a distinguishing factor, the percentage of convicted criminals who are not German citizens is far higher — around 40% — than their share of the population. And they are also reported to the police far more frequently. At the same time, individuals without a German passport are also more likely to become victims of crimes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Pawlik emphasizes that language acquisition is the foundation and starting point of any successful integration. But this is precisely where the government tightened its purse strings earlier this year to save money. Many integration courses are now no longer offered at all or receive less government funding. Pawlik made it clear that she is strongly critical of these cuts, even though she herself is part of the federal government.

Most recently, Pawlik and her fellow Social Democrats have been advocating for people who have been working in Germany for some time to receive more secure residency permits — especially those from Syria and Ukraine. On Tuesday, SPD lawmakers adopted a position paper on the matter. In the paper, they propose that existing legal rights that allow workers to remain in the country should also apply to refugees. In other words, it would give working refugees a more secure status.

But will the conservatives from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) — who lead the coalition led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) — support this? "You'll have to ask the interior minister," Pawlik replied when asked by DW. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) is known for being a hardliner on immigration policy.

This article was originally published in German.

#772. FA explored legal challenge to Infantino staying on

Gianni Infantino has been leading Fifa since 2016

The Football Association has considered challenging Gianni Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, BBC Sport can reveal.

But it believes any attempt to prevent him from standing in the election in March is likely to fail.

Infantino oversaw the introduction of a three-term limit when he replaced Sepp Blatter as leader of world football's governing body.

However, Fifa's council agreed in 2022 that his first period in office from 2016 to 2019 should not count as it was the remainder of his predecessor's interrupted final term.

Earlier this month, human rights campaign group Fair Square wrote to the FA claiming that the decision is open to legal challenge and was "contrary to the spirit and purpose" of Fifa statutes.

It urged the FA to ask Fifa's governance committee to bar Infantino from the election in March because he has already served the maximum three terms.

FA chair Debbie Hewitt has now replied, telling Fair Square that the governing body "has explored the possibility of challenging Mr Infantino's eligibility to run for a further term as the Fifa president but does not consider that such a challenge would secure the outcome sought".

In correspondence seen by the BBC, Hewitt adds: "Ultimately the process followed Fifa's governance and led to an outcome where Mr Infantino's part term was disregarded for the purposes of maximum term limits.

"Having considered the process in detail, we do not believe that a challenge would succeed."

In a statement, Fair Square said: "It's understandable that the FA has no faith in Fifa's internal processes to hold Infantino accountable for serious breaches of the rules, but it's a mistake to abandon these channels, not least because it sends a signal to Infantino that he can do whatever he likes.

"We will encourage the FA to leave its options open where this matter is concerned not least because Debbie Hewitt's position on the Fifa council puts her in a very strong position to demand clear answers on why Fifa discounted Infantino's first term."

Miguel Maduro - a former head of Fifa's governance committee - has said a national association or confederation may need to challenge Infantino's eligibility at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas).

However he has also said that the ability of European football associations to do so has been made harder by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin deciding to stand for a fourth term earlier this year. Ceferin reversed a previous insistence, in 2024, he would not seek re-election.

The FA was among a number of national associations to withdraw its support of Infantino in the wake of the crisis sparked by his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other competitions to private investors.

European confederation Uefa has backed rival candidate Philippe Diallo, the president of the French Football Federation.

Hewitt, who became a member of Fifa's council in 2023, also told Fair Square that the FA "remains opposed to Mr Infantino's re-election and is committed to providing its full support to Philippe Diallo as our preferred candidate in the upcoming Fifa presidential election".

It has previously referred to the fact that in 2022 its council "unanimously confirmed its agreement with the view of the governance, audit & compliance committee that the period between 2016 and 2019 does not count as a term of office for the current Fifa president, who is therefore about to end his first term".

#770. KJ Biermann Accused of 16 Sex Offenses, Including Incest in Prior Case

Prosecutors in the sexual assault case against Kim Zolciak and Kroy Biermann's son KJ shared insight into an April 2025 sexual assault case, in which he was charged with 16 offenses, including incest.

Content warning: This story discusses allegations of sexual assault.

More has come to light about Kroy "KJ" Biermann's legal history.

As the prosecutors in the sexual assault case against the 15-year-old son of Kim Zolciak and Kroy Biermann sought to block the transfer of his case to juvenile court, they detailed 16 previous offenses against the teen from a separate sexual assault case, according to court documents obtained by E! News.

In the response to the defense's motion to transfer the case—KJ was indicted on Sept. 3 on seven counts including aggravated child molestation, aggravated sexual battery, aggravated sodomy, sexual battery against a child under 16 and false imprisonment following an alleged assault on a 15-year-old girl in April—filed with Fulton County Superior Court on Nov. 16, the prosecutors described the previous case as "a very serious one, with probable cause found for incest." (KJ pleaded not guilty to the 2026 case and his attorney Jason Sheffield denied the allegations.)

Prosecutors in the current sexual assault case noted that the 2025 case is currently with the Fulton County Juvenile Court. KJ was charged with incest, eight counts of child molestation, sexual battery, statutory rape and five counts of the sexual exploitation of children in April 2025 after the Milton County Police Department discovered "videos and photos" in a hidden folder on his phone that February.

Sheffield previously addressed the 2025 charges—which he denied on behalf of his client—in a September statement to E! News, accusing the prosecutors on the case of "grossly" misrepresenting the facts.

"The matter arose from inappropriate, crude behavior involving two middle-schoolers," the statement continued. "It did not result in an adjudication for statutory rape, sexual intercourse, or any comparable offense. Any suggestion otherwise is inaccurate and creates a materially misleading impression of how the juvenile matter was ultimately resolved."

E! News has reached out to KJ's attorneys for comment and has not yet heard back. His final plea in the April 2026 case will be entered Feb. 10, according to legal docs.

Prosecutors acquiesced to the goal of the 2025 case being filed through the juvenile legal system was for KJ to "receive the appropriate treatment and rehabilitation to avoid further future crimes or assaults committed by this defendant."

However, the response highlighted that the most recent case—in which the teenage girl, only identified as L.T. in the docs, alleged that she was sexually assaulted by KJ in a Lifetime Fitness gym's changing room—occurred one year after the first.

"This behavior has become part of a deeply troubling pattern when it comes to this defendant forcing sexual compliance through a personal relationship," the response read. "The closeness in time between the two incidents is significant."

"Based on the repetitive pattern of offenses," prosecutors continued, "this defendant has proven to be beyond the rehabilitation offered within the Fulton County Juvenile Court process."

The docs argued that it was "even more concerning" since KJ had completed "all or the vast majority" of his court-mandated therapy sessions at the time of his second alleged offense.

The filing added, "Protection of the community is at the greatest risk when it comes to repeated sexual offenses, regardless of the defendant's age."

The prosecutor's response came two months after Sheffield, who told E! News in September that KJ is "100 percent innocent," requested that his client's case be moved to the juvenile court system due to his age.

"He is an adolescent whose development is ongoing and can demonstrate his ability for understanding, growth and change," the filing, obtained by E! News in September, argued, "and whose future cannot reliably be predicted merely from the labels attached to the allegations against him. The evidence reserved for the transfer hearing will demonstrate that KJ remains amenable to treatment, supervision, structure, education, and rehabilitation within the juvenile justice system."
